title: Cathie Wood’s ARK Sees Tesla at $4,400 With $225B AI Spending Forecast
summary: ARK Invest projects Tesla shares could reach $4,400 in 2031 under a model assuming approximately $225 billion in cumulative AI infrastructure spending. The forecast ties future value to robotaxi services and humanoid robots. AI Spending Assumptions Support the $4,400 Tesla Forecast Cumulative AI inf...
content:
ARK Invest projects Tesla shares could reach $4,400 in 2031 under a model assuming approximately $225 billion in cumulative AI infrastructure spending. The forecast ties future value to robotaxi services and humanoid robots.

Key Takeaways

  • ARK expects robotaxis to contribute 80% of Tesla’s enterprise value in 2031.
  • Its $4,400 target is about 1,039% above the Oct. 21 close.
  • The model incorporates share dilution from Musk’s stock-based compensation.

AI Spending Assumptions Support the $4,400 Tesla Forecast

Cumulative AI infrastructure spending at Tesla would rise from approximately $7 billion at the end of 2025 to $225 billion by the end of 2031 under ARK Invest’s updated Tesla valuation, published Oct. 19. Within the model, higher AI investment improves Optimus productivity. This links computing expenditure to the projected economic output of humanoid robots.

ARK, led by CEO Cathie Wood, stated:

“ARK’s price target for Tesla in 2031 is ~$4,400 per share.”

Shares of Tesla Inc. (Nasdaq: TSLA) closed Oct. 21 at $386.47, up 3.41%, placing ARK’s target approximately 1,039% above that price.

Infrastructure plans include the Tesla-SpaceX Terafab chip project, with an initial $16.8 billion construction commitment in Grimes County, Texas. The planned chips would support autonomous vehicles, robots, and SpaceX’s proposed orbital data centers.

Robotaxis and Optimus Drive the Revenue Projections

Under the illustrative base case, ARK assumes approximately 8.1 million robotaxis, $753 billion in annual ride-hailing net revenue, and $212 billion in Optimus revenue by 2031. Robotaxis would account for approximately 80% of enterprise value, a measure incorporating equity and net debt. The scenario also assumes approximately 1 million Optimus robots sold externally on a cumulative basis by 2031.

At equal utilization rates, ARK estimates Tesla’s operating costs per mile could be approximately 40% below those of Waymo’s next-generation robotaxi. Its analysis links the advantage to vertical integration and camera-based autonomous driving. Consumer-owned vehicles could expand the fleet, while lower fares could broaden demand beyond current ride-hailing users.

These projections align with CEO Elon Musk’s expectations for Optimus and Cybercab. In an Oct. 18 X post, Musk identified the humanoid robot and purpose-built driverless vehicle as the sources of most of Tesla’s future value.

Tesla reported 486,532 vehicle deliveries and 13.7 gigawatt-hours of storage deployments for the third quarter in its Oct. 2 announcement. It also listed production of 464,391 vehicles. Model 3 and Model Y vehicles accounted for 478,237 deliveries, while other models contributed 8,295. The figures provide an operating baseline for comparison with ARK’s projections.

Dilution and Deployment Risks Shape the Valuation

Bear and bull estimates of approximately $3,300 and $5,000 per share correspond to the simulation’s 25th and 75th percentiles. These are positions within a distribution of modeled outcomes, rather than minimum and maximum prices. Results below the bear estimate and above the bull estimate remain possible.

Monte Carlo simulation tests combinations of assumptions across 32 independent inputs. Those inputs determine projected operations and share valuations. Share count also affects the value attributable to each investor’s equity ownership stake. ARK assumes Musk’s stock-based compensation vests within the forecast period, incorporating the resulting dilution into its valuation.

A possible SpaceX combination receives separate consideration from ARK’s standalone Tesla model, following earlier Tesla-SpaceX merger speculation. Investor Steve Eisman questioned such a deal’s appeal for SpaceX shareholders during a June 8 CNBC interview.

Musk said during SpaceX’s Oct. 20 earnings call that both companies have formed special committees to discuss a merger, calling a combination a “good idea.” He added that he will stay out of those talks as a conflicted party. Regulatory delays and slower robotaxi expansion remain risks to ARK’s forecast. The firm also identifies Musk’s sudden departure, natural disasters, and a pandemic as events that could disrupt the deployment assumptions.

title: PHP Foundation admits ‘structural failure’ delayed critical security fix
summary: Government websites and online services were disrupted after concerns about a PHP bug that could allow attackers to take control of vulnerable servers.
content:
The PHP Foundation has acknowledged that indecision and a shortage of resources delayed a fix for a critical security flaw first identified in 2024, calling the stalled response a “structural failure.” 

Government agencies and other organizations worldwide took websites offline Wednesday as a precaution while PHP released emergency patches for two related critical vulnerabilities. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on affected servers without logging in. 

PHP is a programming language widely used to power websites and web applications, including content management systems. 

In a blog post following the release of the patch, the foundation described how its developers first found signs of the vulnerability in 2024, but struggled to come up with a solution without disrupting the large ecosystem of software built using PHP.

“Combined with the lack of a known path to remote code execution and the small team of core developers with the necessary deep knowledge of the engine occupied with many responsibilities, this decision process caused work on a fix to stall and restart repeatedly over months,” said the foundation.

“We won’t pretend otherwise: the delay was a structural failure, caused by both the security team’s decision process and its lack of resources.”

The foundation was pointed to the vulnerability again on August 11, after security firm Calif and OpenAI independently reported the same underlying issue, with Calif demonstrating unconditional remote code execution, which made it a top security priority. 

Websites go dark amid PHP security scare

The disruption stretched across the world as developers disconnected websites while preparing to install the emergency fixes.

The Netherlands shut its digital identity service, and the country’s National Cyber Security Center also took its website offline. 

Finland’s state IT provider Valtori disconnected government public web services, while France’s Interior Ministry temporarily took prefecture websites offline. Germany’s federal IT provider ITZBund also disabled several websites, according to Reuters. 

In Australia, the Australian Signals Directorate acknowledged that its cybersecurity website, cyber.gov.au, was among government sites affected by the PHP issue.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi took to X to urge website operators to prepare to apply the patch as quickly as possible. In a post, she said temporarily suspending website functions could reduce the risk if the patch couldn’t be applied immediately. 

The Wikimedia Foundation, which operates Wikipedia, said it took some supporting services offline as a precaution, including Toolforge and Cloud VPS, which host tools and projects used by volunteer developers, leading to parts of Wikipedia going offline on Wednesday. 

Blockchain security firm SlowMist said its MistEye service surveyed PHP use across the crypto industry, urging exchanges, DeFi platforms and wallet providers to review their exposure and upgrade. It identified 793 domains with direct PHP fingerprints among 1,488 domains assessed.

Intersect, a membership organization supporting the Cardano blockchain’s development and governance, said it had temporarily taken its Members Area offline while it assessed potential exposure. The page is still offline at the time of writing. 

Related: Tech giants rush to block 8 eMudhra certs that could enable fake sites 

Coinbase chief security officer Jeff Lunglhofer said the company found no evidence of any exposed PHP instances. 

“Whenever we hear about vulnerabilities like this, we automatically conduct a full sweep to make sure everything is as safe as we can make it. We’re also working with our third party suppliers for extra assurance.”

Digital asset infrastructure company BitGo also said its platform was unaffected by the PHP vulnerability. 

Meanwhile, Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao warned internet users on Wednesday to be “extra careful” visiting any website in the next few days, as some web administrators may not be up-to-date with security patches. 

OpenAI has released a Codex skill to help website operators check for potentially vulnerable PHP versions and identify applicable updates, which can be accessed via GitHub. 

The PHP security team said it has not identified any functional exploits at the time of its public disclosure.

title: Robert Kiyosaki Sees Major Economic Reset as AI Threatens Job Security
summary: Robert Kiyosaki argues that artificial intelligence is challenging the traditional route from education to secure employment. The Rich Dad Poor Dad author warns the disruption could form part of one of history’s greatest economic resets. Robert Kiyosaki Questions the Promise of a High-Paying Job Art...
content:
Robert Kiyosaki argues that artificial intelligence is challenging the traditional route from education to secure employment. The Rich Dad Poor Dad author warns the disruption could form part of one of history’s greatest economic resets.

Key Takeaways

  • Kiyosaki identifies doctors, lawyers, and accountants as exposed to AI.
  • His reset argument questions whether established career advice still works.
  • He encourages followers to evaluate his views and reach their own answers.

Robert Kiyosaki Questions the Promise of a High-Paying Job

Artificial intelligence could undermine the job security associated with advanced education, author and financial educator Robert Kiyosaki warned. In an Oct. 21 warning about AI and job security on X, he questioned whether familiar career guidance still prepares people for technological change.

Kiyosaki challenged advice that has shaped education and employment decisions for generations, asking whether it remains useful as AI advances. Questioning whether AI is making the following career advice obsolete, he wrote:

“Go to school, get good grades, so you can get a high paying job!”

He defined a reset as a change in which methods that worked previously will no longer work in the future. To illustrate that transition, he compared AI with cars replacing horses and Amazon disrupting shopping malls. Doctors, lawyers, and accountants were among the professions he characterized as already facing replacement by the technology.

Princeton Job Search Highlights Pressure on Graduates

A Princeton graduate’s prolonged search for employment supplied the example Kiyosaki used to question the relationship between advanced education and opportunity. The Wall Street Journal’s account of the graduate’s search described more than 2,300 applications by Jack Weis, who earned a chemical engineering doctorate in 2024.

The Journal detailed applications spanning corporate science, postdoctoral fellowships, software engineering, and food preparation, alongside temporary work training AI. Kiyosaki attributed most employers’ decisions to AI replacing highly educated staff.

The famous author’s latest position extends his earlier warning about AI replacing employees while creating opportunities for business owners. In February, he argued that entrepreneurs could use the technology to increase their wealth as workers faced displacement. That distinction places ownership and adaptability at the center of his economic outlook.

Economic Reset Argument Extends Beyond Employment

Independent judgment also features in Kiyosaki’s emphasis on financial education over financial advice during an Oct. 7 Rich Dad Radio Show discussion. He encouraged followers to develop the knowledge to evaluate opportunities for themselves, a position echoed in his latest invitation to question his views.

His broader economic crash warning has linked AI speculation with debt, conflict, and population aging. Those concerns extend his argument beyond employment to the financial pressures facing savers and investors.

The renowned author’s preferred holdings include businesses, income-producing property, gold, silver, and bitcoin, a digital currency that operates through a decentralized network. He has presented that mix as his approach to preparing for financial disruption.

In July, Kiyosaki described how he would start over financially if he lost everything and had only $10,000 left. His hypothetical $10,000 rebuilding plan began with paying for financial education and mentorship before buying investments. He would then develop skills in sales, marketing, and communication.

title: Ripple-Backed Evernorth Eyes $132M Funding Amid XRP Buying Plans
summary: Evernorth plans to raise capital to buy more XRP, while existing warrants could provide up to $132.2 million in additional funding. Its latest prospectus details the cash investments and token contributions that helped establish its treasury. Evernorth Plans Further XRP Purchases Through Capital Rai...
content:
Evernorth plans to raise capital to buy more XRP, while existing warrants could provide up to $132.2 million in additional funding. Its latest prospectus details the cash investments and token contributions that helped establish its treasury.

Key Takeaways

  • Full cash exercise of public warrants could generate about $132.2 million.
  • Completed advance and delayed placements brought $224.55 million in cash.
  • Ripple contributed 126,791,458 XRP to Evernorth’s operating subsidiary.

Evernorth Plans Further XRP Purchases Through Capital Raising

Buying additional XRP forms part of the financing strategy that Evernorth Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: XRPN) outlined in its Oct. 19 prospectus. The XRP treasury company registered 11,499,992 Class A shares issuable through existing public warrants, which give holders the right to purchase stock at $11.50 per share. Full cash exercise would generate approximately $132.2 million.

Describing how it intends to expand its holdings, Evernorth stated:

“We intend to raise capital using a variety of structures determined by market conditions and to purchase XRP with the proceeds through trading protocols designed to minimize slippage.”

Slippage is the difference between an expected trading price and the price actually obtained. The prospectus gives management discretion to use any net proceeds for general corporate purposes. Receiving that money depends on holders exercising their purchase rights for cash. The company noted: “There is no assurance that the holders of the public warrants will elect to exercise any or all of such warrants.”

Cash Investments and XRP Contributions Established the Treasury

Potential warrant receipts would supplement financing completed when Evernorth entered public markets with approximately 473 million XRP and about $300 million in gross cash proceeds before transaction expenses. Its completed business combination closed Oct. 9, bringing together cash subscriptions and direct contributions of XRP in exchange for equity.

Investors contributed a combined $224.55 million in cash and 800,000 XRP through two private placements in exchange for Evernorth shares. Both transactions closed with the merger on Oct. 9, following an administrative delay that changed the company’s merger and trading schedule.

Other investors provided XRP directly in exchange for ownership stakes in Evernorth or its operating subsidiary, Pathfinder Digital Assets LLC. These cryptocurrency contributions included approximately 211.3 million XRP from transaction sponsor Arrington XRP Capital Fund LP, 50 million XRP from Ripple-affiliated Larsen Lam Children’s Remainder Trust, and 126.8 million XRP from Ripple.

Additional Funding Would Also Increase the Share Count

For shareholders, warrant exercises would increase both available capital and the number of outstanding shares. Evernorth’s Nasdaq-listed common stock trades under XRPN, with warrants listed separately as XRPNW. The public warrants became exercisable upon the Oct. 9 closing, subject to registration requirements, and expire five years afterward unless redeemed earlier. Issuing shares would dilute existing shareholders’ ownership percentages.

The warrant terms also determine how those purchase rights can be settled. Evernorth can redeem warrants for one cent each with at least 30 days’ notice if specified $18 trading-price conditions are met. Certain registration-related circumstances permit cashless exercise, allowing holders to surrender warrants for a reduced number of shares without paying cash. Such exercises would generate no cash proceeds.

Changes in outstanding stock also affect Evernorth’s objective of increasing XRP holdings per share, which the company emphasized as it marked its Nasdaq listing on Oct. 14. Progress toward that objective depends on treasury growth relative to the share count.

Alongside further purchases, Evernorth plans to put portions of its existing treasury to work through institutional investment strategies. Its XRP deployment plans with Ripple, Coinbase, Kraken, and Bitgo target the fourth quarter, with partnership agreements subject to customary closing conditions and required regulatory and corporate approvals.

No, you cannot use a BingX invite code if you already have an existing account. The referral code must be entered during the sign-up process for new accounts. Once you’re registered, you cannot retroactively apply an invite code to an old account.

title: Qubic Restarts Chain as Victims Seek $1.3 Million in Stolen QU
summary: Qubic’s blockchain is back online after a thief drained 1,404 wallets of nearly $1.3 million, forcing the network into an emergency shutdown. Now, with stolen funds frozen and a recovery program underway, victims have a chance to reclaim their cryptocurrency. Qubic Resumes Operations After 1,404 Wal...
content:
Qubic’s blockchain is back online after a thief drained 1,404 wallets of nearly $1.3 million, forcing the network into an emergency shutdown. Now, with stolen funds frozen and a recovery program underway, victims have a chance to reclaim their cryptocurrency.

Key Takeaways

  • Qubic restarted its blockchain after attackers drained 1,404 wallets of approximately $1.3 million.
  • Qubic’s validators approved a recovery plan, with verified victims already receiving payments.
  • Qubic victims have until May 1, 2027, to file claims for stolen cryptocurrency.

Qubic Resumes Operations After 1,404 Wallets Are Drained

Qubic has restarted its blockchain following the Oct. 18 security incident that saw approximately 2.94 trillion QU tokens stolen in less than two hours. The network’s validators, known as Computors, had stopped transactions at tick 85,371,949 to prevent further losses.

By the evening of Oct. 19, the blockchain was processing transactions again. On Oct. 20, Qubic announced that its validators had approved a recovery plan, opened a claims portal and begun sending payments to verified victims.

The attack didn’t involve breaking Qubic’s blockchain. Instead, the thief exploited weak wallet recovery seeds, the secret strings of characters that give owners access to their cryptocurrency.

An Apple Software Weakness Left Wallets Exposed

The problem centered on how certain wallets created those secret recovery strings. Older versions of Qubic’s wallet software used a random-number generator that wasn’t secure enough to protect cryptocurrency.

The flaw affected wallets created through browsers on iPhones and iPads, Safari on Macs, and older versions of Qubic’s iOS application. Attackers could potentially reconstruct predictable recovery seeds and gain access without knowing the owner’s password. Qubic said it corrected the problem in wallet version 4.26.4, released around Oct. 19, replacing the weak generator with a more secure method.

However, updating the software doesn’t repair an old recovery seed. Anyone who created a wallet using the affected software must generate an entirely new wallet and transfer their funds. Simply opening the old wallet on another device won’t make it safe.

Stolen Funds Frozen as Qubic Opens Recovery Claims

The thief’s escape plan hit a wall when Qubic halted its network. Approximately 87.1% of the stolen tokens remained trapped on the blockchain, while cryptocurrency exchange MEXC froze an account holding the remaining 12.9%. Qubic subsequently placed affected onchain funds into protected escrow, allowing its validators to begin returning cryptocurrency to verified owners.

The team said victims can submit claims through Qubic’s official recovery portal until May 1, 2027. Applicants must provide their affected wallet identity, a newly generated destination wallet, a signed ownership message, and supporting evidence. Approved claims face a seven-day dispute period before payment. Recovery of funds held at MEXC depends on the exchange and any law-enforcement proceedings.

Qubic has also warned users that legitimate recovery assistance never requires surrendering a wallet seed or paying a fee. The blockchain is moving again, but the incident leaves an uncomfortable question for cryptocurrency holders. What good is an uncompromised blockchain when the software protecting its wallets can hand an attacker the keys?

title: American Bankers Association: OCC’s GENIUS rules ‘undermine’ US Congress
summary: Banking advocacy organizations are pushing back against the OCC’s finalized rules on a stablecoin law, arguing against changes to provisions on yield.
content:
A lobbying group for US banks has weighed in on the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency’s (OCC’s) recently finalized rules on payment stablecoin issuance and custody, arguing that the regulator’s interpretation went against Congress’ intent.

In a Wednesday notice, the American Bankers Association (ABA) said that while the OCC’s final rules implementing the GENIUS Act included “several positive steps,” the banking group remained critical of provisions related to stablecoin yield. The regulator dropped a provision that would have established a presumption that certain third-party arrangements violated the law’s ban on yield payments.

“The final rule removes the OCC’s originally proposed safeguards that would have addressed indirect arrangements involving affiliates, exchanges and other distribution partners,” said ABA. “As a result, payment stablecoin issuers can provide economically equivalent yield while technically avoiding the statutory prohibition. The OCC also declined to adopt a broader presumption against arrangements designed to circumvent the ban.”

The group added:

“Those gaps risk undermining the distinction Congress drew between payment stablecoins and traditional bank deposits, threatening the funds banks use to make the loans that drive the US economy.”

Stablecoin rewards were one of the key issues lawmakers and interest groups debated before and after GENIUS passed Congress in July 2025, and they continue to face scrutiny amid discussions of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, a crypto market structure bill currently in limbo after a failed procedure vote in the Senate last month.

Notably, the Blockchain Association approved of the change to yield prohibition, arguing that the OCC “[brought] the final rule more closely in line with the statutory text.” The Bank Policy Institute, another banking industry advocacy group, largely sided with ABA, saying that “the decision to omit the yield presumption replaces clarity with ambiguity and puts the banking system and its customers at risk of deposit flight.”

The OCC finalized its rules ahead of the GENIUS Act’s implementation in January 2027. Other government departments are expected to release rules on GENIUS related to their agencies’ purview over stablecoins, including the Federal Reserve and Treasury.

Related: ABA, state banking groups push back on CLARITY Act stablecoin yield provisions

title: CME Posts Record Q3 Revenue Despite Lower Daily Trading Volume
summary:
CME Group handled fewer futures and options contracts per day in Q3 than in Q2, but more over the quarter as a whole. That difference helped it post its highest third-quarter revenue on record, even as the average amount earned per contract barely changed.
London's trading industry is coming home!
T...
content:
2026-10-21T23:50:00.000+02:00

Wednesday, 21/10/2026 | 21:50 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Two extra trading days turned a 1.3% decline in ADV from Q2 into an estimated 1.8% increase in total futures and options contracts.
  • CME estimates that fee changes effective in October could add 0.5%–1% to clearing and transaction revenue over a full year at similar trading levels.

CME Group handled fewer futures and options contracts per day in Q3 than in Q2, but more over the quarter as a whole. That difference helped it post its highest third-quarter revenue on record, even as the average amount earned per contract barely changed.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The difference between lower daily activity and higher quarterly revenue largely reflects the calendar. Q3 contained 64 trading days, two more than Q2.

Based on CME’s reported ADV, approximately 1.88 billion futures and options contracts traded during Q3, up from around 1.85 billion in the previous quarter.

MetricQ2 2026Q3 2026Quarterly change
Revenue$1.706bn$1.737bn+1.8%
Clearing and transaction fees$1.353bn$1.378bn+1.9%
Futures and options ADV29.84m29.45m-1.3%
Trading days6264+2 days
Estimated futures and options contracts traded1.85bn1.88bn+1.8%
Average rate per futures and options contract$0.678$0.679Broadly flat
Adjusted net income$1.082bn$1.084bn+0.2

More Contracts at a Similar Average Rate

Clearing and transaction fees, CME’s main revenue source, rose nearly 2% to $1.38 billion. That was close to the estimated increase in futures and options contracts traded, although the fee figure also includes cash-market activity through EBS and BrokerTec and is not directly interchangeable with contract volume.

The average rate per futures and options contract moved only slightly, from $0.678 to $0.679. It remained below the $0.702 reported in Q3 2025, so a higher average rate did not materially drive the sequential revenue increase.

CME said the small rise from Q2 reflected changes in volume-based discounts and a lower proportion of micro contracts. CME’s earnings commentary.

The mix of contracts changed even though the overall rate remained nearly flat. Interest-rate ADV rose from 14.5 million to 15.1 million contracts, while equity-index ADV declined from 8.6 million to 7.7 million.

Daily volumes in foreign exchange, energy, agriculture and metals were broadly stable or slightly lower. Beyond transaction fees, revenue from data and information services rose by $5 million from Q2 to a record $243 million. That was 20% above Q3 2025.

New Products and the Next Revenue Test

CME Group launched several contracts during the quarter, extending its product range from smaller positions for retail traders to new ways for institutions to trade credit exposure.

On August 24, the exchange introduced E-nano futures on four US equity indices. At one-tenth the size of Micro E-minis, they reduce the minimum exposure needed to trade the S&P 500, Nasdaq-100, Russell 2000 and Dow Jones benchmarks.

CME then began trading futures linked to the S&P UBS USD Liquid Leveraged Loan Index on September 14. These give institutions an exchange-traded alternative for managing leveraged-loan exposure, with potential margin offsets against other positions cleared at CME.

The contract joins CME’s wider credit futures suite, where open interest exceeded $2 billion in September. Beyond new contract listings, CME plans to begin clearing cash Treasury transactions and repos on December 7.

The service would expand its post-trade business ahead of the SEC’s central-clearing mandate. Most of the new contracts arrived late in Q3, and CME has not disclosed their revenue contribution.

The quarter’s result is therefore better explained by more trading days and stronger market-data sales than by the new listings.

Transaction-fee changes took effect on October 1; CME estimates they would add 0.5% to 1% to clearing and transaction fees on a full-year basis at similar activity levels.

Their effect will first appear in Q4 results, giving readers another factor to weigh alongside trading volume and the number of trading days.

title: Stablecoin Laundering Network Lands Colombian Crypto Broker in Prison
summary: A Colombian cryptocurrency broker known as “Rey” has been sentenced to 160 months in federal prison for helping launder $14.5 million in drug proceeds using Tether’s USDT and participating in a cocaine importation conspiracy. The operation connected Colombian drug traffickers, an unlicensed American...
content:
A Colombian cryptocurrency broker known as “Rey” has been sentenced to 160 months in federal prison for helping launder $14.5 million in drug proceeds using Tether’s USDT and participating in a cocaine importation conspiracy. The operation connected Colombian drug traffickers, an unlicensed American crypto exchange, and a web of shell companies. Prosecutors also secured a $14.75 million forfeiture order, while five co-defendants received prison sentences.

Key Takeaways

  • Colombian crypto broker Leonardo Zuluaga Duque received 160 months in prison for laundering drug proceeds.
  • Prosecutors traced $14.5 million in Tether’s USDT through American shell companies and Colombian businesses.
  • Maximilien de Hoop Cartier’s unlicensed crypto operation transmitted more than $470 million in illicit proceeds.

Colombian Crypto Broker Gets 160 Months as USDT-Centric Drug Network Unravels

The operation has landed the broker more than 13 years behind bars. On Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026, federal prosecutors announced that Leonardo de Jesus Zuluaga Duque, 63, received a 160-month prison sentence for his role in laundering approximately $14.5 million and conspiring to import cocaine into the United States. The case also exposed a much larger financial operation handling hundreds of millions of dollars.

From Colombian Drug Money to American Bank Accounts

Between May and November 2023, Zuluaga Duque worked alongside several associates to move roughly $14.5 million in drug trafficking proceeds through a cross-border cryptocurrency laundering network.

The operation had a straightforward financial playbook. Criminal proceeds were converted into the stablecoin USDT in Colombia, transferred to an American intermediary and exchanged for U.S. dollars. Those dollars then traveled through American shell companies before returning to Colombian businesses, where they were converted into pesos and distributed. At the center of the American operation was Maximilien de Hoop Cartier, an Argentine citizen who claimed connections to the famous Cartier jewelry dynasty.

Cartier operated an unlicensed cryptocurrency money-transmitting business through companies presented to banks as legitimate technology enterprises. Prosecutors stated that his operation processed more than $470 million in illicit proceeds, far exceeding the $14.5 million directly attributed to Zuluaga Duque’s laundering activities. Cartier previously pleaded guilty and received eight years in federal prison.

Cocaine Conspiracy Blows the Case Wide Open

The crypto transactions were only half the trouble. Federal investigators also connected Zuluaga Duque to an operation intended to bring cocaine from Colombia into New York. In November 2023, confidential sources working with law enforcement arranged a transaction involving approximately nine kilograms of cocaine paste. Prosecutors said the material was intended for processing into cocaine before delivery to the state of New York.

Adrian Fernando Areiza Ceballos delivered the narcotics to an undercover officer, while Zuluaga Duque collected a commission for helping arrange the transaction. The operation continued into February 2024, when investigators arranged another prospective purchase involving approximately 100 kilograms of cocaine paste. Colombian police subsequently executed search warrants and recovered roughly 111 kilograms.

By then, the heat was on. Colombian authorities arrested Zuluaga Duque and other defendants in Medellín on April 30, 2024, with the assistance of Interpol.

Prosecutors Crack Down on International Crypto Laundering

U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald said the defendants exploited cryptocurrency, shell companies and traditional banking channels to move criminal proceeds across international borders. McDonald stated:

“The defendant and his conspirators operated a sophisticated international scheme to utilize cryptocurrency, a network of shell companies in the U.S. and Colombia, and numerous crypto accounts.”

The federal judge ordered Zuluaga Duque to forfeit $14,751,846, along with cryptocurrency associated with four addresses under his control. He also received five years of supervised release. All five co-defendants have now been sentenced, with prison terms ranging from three to eight years.

The case carries an awkward distinction for anyone portraying cryptocurrency as the entire laundering mechanism: The USDT transfers moved the value across borders, but conventional banks, shell companies and dollar transactions were indispensable to turning that value back into spendable Colombian pesos.

title: Strive, Strategy Shares Jump as Bitcoin Price Eyes $85K
summary: Shares of bitcoin treasury companies Strategy and Strive surged Wednesday, extending gains as bitcoin rebounded to hit its highest price in two weeks and investors weighed fresh BTC acquisitions and financing moves by the two publicly traded firms. Bitcoin Bounceback Boosts Big Buyers Strategy (Nasd...
content:
Shares of bitcoin treasury companies Strategy and Strive surged Wednesday, extending gains as bitcoin rebounded to hit its highest price in two weeks and investors weighed fresh BTC acquisitions and financing moves by the two publicly traded firms.

Key Takeaways

  • Strategy (MSTR) rose over 7%, while Strive (ASST) jumped more than 13% Wednesday amid bitcoin’s rebound.
  • Strategy acquired another 267 BTC for $22.1 million last week, bringing its holdings to 848,517 BTC.
  • Strive recently purchased 4,045 BTC, reaching 36,818 BTC, and raised $630 million through a new preferred stock offering.

Bitcoin Bounceback Boosts Big Buyers

Strategy (Nasdaq: MSTR), the largest corporate holder of bitcoin with over $71 billion in holdings, climbed more than 7% to finish at $153.48 on Wednesday, while Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) jumped more than 13% to finish at $30.75, per data from Yahoo Finance.

The gains followed another strong session Tuesday, when Strategy rose nearly 5%, and Strive advanced nearly 6%. Strive also gained 6% Monday, giving the firm three straight days of green so far this week.

The rally came as bitcoin climbed more than 2% to trade around $84,500, providing a boost to companies whose equity valuations are closely tied to the cryptocurrency’s performance. The price of bitcoin rose as high as $84,807 on Wednesday afternoon (E.T.), marking the coin’s highest price since October 7 as it eyed a potential return above the $85,000 mark.

Both companies have recently expanded their bitcoin holdings while pursuing different approaches to raising capital and managing their balance sheets.

Strategy disclosed Monday that it purchased another 267 BTC for approximately $22.1 million between Oct. 12 and Oct. 18, bringing its total holdings to 848,517 BTC. The company paid an average of $82,900 per coin in its latest acquisition, financing the purchase primarily through sales of 140,872 common shares.

Strategy also revealed that it repurchased approximately $193.1 million of its STRC preferred shares and expanded its digital credit securities repurchase authorization from $2 billion to $3 billion. The company reported approximately $5.28 billion in dollar-denominated assets, including reserves intended to support preferred dividends and debt interest payments.

Strive Goes Into Overdrive

Meanwhile, Strive has been pursuing an aggressive bitcoin accumulation strategy of its own, alongside the launch of a new preferred stock designed to generate additional capital.

The Dallas-based company acquired 4,045 BTC between Oct. 12 and Oct. 16, bringing its total holdings to 36,818 BTC, valued at roughly $3.1 billion at recent market prices.

On Tuesday, Strive launched its new Series A Perpetual Preferred Stock, trading under the ticker SATS, after raising $630 million through an upsized offering of 7 million shares priced at $90 each.

The securities carry a 15% annual dividend on their $100 stated value, translating to an effective yield of approximately 16.7% at the offering price. Strive plans to distribute cash dividends every business day beginning Nov. 9, subject to board approval and available funds. The proceeds may support further bitcoin acquisitions, working capital, income-producing investments, and share repurchases.

The rallies highlight renewed investor interest in publicly traded bitcoin treasury companies, which offer stock market exposure to the cryptocurrency while introducing additional risks associated with corporate financing, dividend obligations, and potential shareholder dilution.

For both Strategy and Strive, rising bitcoin prices can boost the market value of their holdings and improve the appeal of their fundraising strategies. But the same mechanisms can amplify losses when the cryptocurrency declines, leaving shareholders exposed to volatility beyond bitcoin’s price movements alone.

Strategy felt that pain acutely this summer when its shares fell to a price of about $82 as its treasury holdings sat underwater and investors’ concerns over constant accumulation grew even louder. But the firm has since clawed back all of its losses so far this year, showing a roughly 1% gain in price since the start of 2026.

title: Three Companies Have Notified the SEC of Intention To Start Tokenized Stocks Trading
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Three Companies Have Notified the SEC of Intention To Start Tokenized Stocks Trading
The Securities and Exchange Commission is taking applications from companies wanting to list tokenized stocks. 
This post Three Companies Have Notified the SEC of Intention To Start Tokenized Stock...
content:
Three companies have notified the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission of their plans to operate tokenized securities venues following a new rule, according to the top regulator. 

Tokenized Stock Venue, Perpetuals.com, and OKX have all submitted plans to operate by allowing trading of tokenized stocks, the SEC said in a Wednesday announcement. 

Along with the Intercontinental Exchange, crypto exchange OKX was the first to file with the regulator to debut tokenized securities trading on a new platform, OKXICE. 

The SEC in September said it was offering a five-year exemption to platforms that facilitate trading of tokenized stocks. Regulators like the SEC are pushing ahead with regulating the crypto space despite lawmakers blocking major digital asset legislation in September. 

Tokenized stocks are the latest example of firms wanting to utilize Bitcoin’s underlying technology to help upgrade traditional finance. By putting stocks on the blockchain, traders can operate 24/7, according to proponents. 

The SEC said Wednesday that just because the firms are on the list, doesn’t necessarily mean they meet all the requirements for the rule. 

Wall Street’s top regulator is now very pro-crypto under U.S. President Donald Trump. SEC Chair Paul Atkins has said the regulator wants to “update” how it watchdogs securities, and “modernize them in the age of blockchain and crypto assets.”

Atkins has said that the regulator wants the U.S. to be on track to be the “crypto capital of the world.” 

Under the previous Democratic Joe Biden administration, the SEC was hostile towards the crypto industry and hit major companies — including Coinbase and Kraken — with lawsuits. The regulator attracted criticism for so-called regulation by enforcement. 

But under Trump, that has changed: the Republican campaigned on a ticket to help the crypto space and has signed a number of laws and executive orders aimed at helping the digital asset space. 

Traditional finance titans like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton for years have used blockchain rails to tokenize money funds.

In January, the S&P 500 gave crypto platform Trade[XYZ] the green light to debut a new derivative contract on decentralized exchange Hyperliquid, giving traders the ability to trade the stock index 24-7. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: CFTC Slaps $9.2 Million Fine and Lifetime Ban on NOLA FX Founder
summary:
A Ponzi-style forex scheme has left its organiser facing nearly $16 million in court-ordered payments.


That comes on top of the $6,748,412 in restitution DePetrillo was ordered to pay victims when he received a nine-year prison sentence in July 2025.


Fake Forex Profits Concealed Diverted Funds

...
content:
2026-10-21T22:35:00.000+02:00

Wednesday, 21/10/2026 | 20:35 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • The civil judgment permanently bars DePetrillo and his companies from CFTC-regulated markets.
  • The CFTC has alleged similar practices in other forex and crypto cases this year.

A Ponzi-style forex scheme has left its organiser facing nearly $16 million in court-ordered payments.

The U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Louisiana ordered Michael B. DePetrillo and his companies, Meteor LLC and NOLA FX Capital Management LLC, to pay a $9,211,492 civil monetary penalty for their participation in the fraudulent retail forex operation.

That comes on top of the $6,748,412 in restitution DePetrillo was ordered to pay victims when he received a nine-year prison sentence in July 2025.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission said the default judgment resolves its civil case. It also permanently bars the three defendants from trading in CFTC-regulated markets or registering with the agency.

Fake Forex Profits Concealed Diverted Funds

The operation used a familiar Ponzi-style mechanism behind a forex-trading pitch. DePetrillo and his companies told investors they would pool their money in the NOLA FX Fund and use it to trade leveraged currency contracts.

Instead, contributions from new investors helped pay earlier participants, while false account statements presented the fund as a profitable forex operation.

According to the Justice Department, DePetrillo collected approximately $9.2 million from around 55 investors over seven years. In the civil case, the court found that the defendants had misappropriated more than $3 million of participant funds, using the money for those payouts, DePetrillo’s personal expenses and trading in his own accounts.

DePetrillo pleaded guilty in February 2025. At his sentencing, the court imposed the nine-year prison term and ordered him to pay $6,748,412 in restitution to victims.

CFTC Pursues Other Forex and Crypto Fraud Cases

The DePetrillo judgment is one of several CFTC actions this year involving investment pools presented as trading businesses.

In August, the regulator sued Goliath Ventures, alleging that it took at least $397 million for cryptocurrency trading while issuing statements showing profits that did not exist.

The following month, the CFTC brought a case against Cash FX Group. It alleged that the company collected more than $950 million for a purported forex trading pool, conducted little trading and used new deposits to pay earlier participants.

The Goliath and Cash FX figures remain allegations in the CFTC’s lawsuits. DePetrillo’s case has reached a different stage: a criminal sentence and restitution order were already in place, and the new judgment closes the regulator’s civil action.

The following month, the CFTC brought a case against Cash FX Group. It alleged that the company collected more than $950 million for a purported forex trading pool, conducted little trading and used new deposits to pay earlier participants.

The Goliath and Cash FX figures remain allegations in the CFTC’s lawsuits. DePetrillo’s case has reached a different stage: a criminal sentence and restitution order were already in place, and the new judgment closes the regulator’s civil action.

title: Ethereum and Arbitrum Gain New Privacy Layer as Fhenix Goes Live
summary: Fhenix has launched its mainnet alongside its fully homomorphic encryption coprocessor, enabling smart contracts to execute directly on encrypted data while enforcing rules onchain. Offchain Computation and Dual-Mode Tokens Fhenix launched its mainnet on Ethereum and Layer 2 network Arbitrum on Oct....
content:
Fhenix has launched its mainnet alongside its fully homomorphic encryption coprocessor, enabling smart contracts to execute directly on encrypted data while enforcing rules onchain.

Key Takeaways

  • Fhenix launched its CoFHE mainnet on Ethereum and Arbitrum to execute encrypted smart contract operations.
  • Offchain Labs CEO Steven Goldfeder highlighted that CoFHE solves institutional privacy needs in DeFi.
  • Fhenix plans to deploy three decentralized apps in Q4 while expanding confidential applications to Solana via hackathons.

Offchain Computation and Dual-Mode Tokens

Fhenix launched its mainnet on Ethereum and Layer 2 network Arbitrum on Oct. 21, bringing its fully homomorphic encryption coprocessor, CoFHE, into production to allow smart contracts to compute on encrypted data without exposing sensitive information onchain.

The technology enables smart contracts across both blockchain networks to process encrypted figures directly, keeping account balances, positions, and trading strategies confidential while preserving automated rule enforcement.

The launch aims to address a long-standing privacy hurdle in decentralized finance (DeFi) by allowing institutional investors and developers to execute transactions without broadcasting sensitive strategies to the public ledger.

“Confidentiality is one of the biggest barriers between institutions and public blockchains,” said Steven Goldfeder, co-founder and CEO of Offchain Labs, the developer behind Arbitrum. “They need to keep positions and strategies private, and until now that meant giving up the composability that makes onchain markets worth using.”

Fhenix’s coprocessor offloads intensive encrypted computation off-chain before returning verified results to smart contracts on Ethereum and Arbitrum. The system features a dynamic throughput design that scales processing capacity with demand, along with a dual-mode feature allowing users to toggle token balances between public and confidential modes within a single transaction—without wrapping or bridging assets.

Initial Ecosystem and Security Audits

The platform launches with two initial design partners: Fluton, an encrypted intent engine for cross-chain transactions, and Alpha Engine, a financial network where strategists submit encrypted trading strategies to compete for liquidity.

Ahead of the deployment, blockchain security firm Consensys Diligence completed a technical audit of the system.

“An entire market can clear on numbers nobody has ever seen, the contract running it included, and the outcome is still correct and still checkable by anyone,” Consensys Diligence said in a statement. “The category of application waiting on the other side simply was not available before.”

Looking ahead, Fhenix plans to deploy three additional decentralized applications (dapps) on CoFHE in the fourth quarter and announce two institutional strategic partnerships in the coming weeks. The company is also developing a confidential stablecoin in collaboration with Tandem and participating in the Colosseum hackathon to explore demand for confidential applications on the Solana blockchain.

“CoFHE is now live on Ethereum and Arbitrum mainnet, with competitive performance and a UX that’s simple for any builder who wants privacy in their dapp,” remarked Guy Zyskind, founder of Fhenix.

title: Tether backs Bolivian fintech bringing USDT payments to food delivery and banking
summary: The investment will support Peso’s expansion across four Latin American markets, where it connects stablecoin payments to merchant services and local banking networks.
content:
Tether has led a pre-seed funding round in Bolivian fintech Peso, which offers USDT payments through food delivery apps and local banking networks, to support the company’s expansion across Latin America.

In a Wednesday announcement, Tether said the investment will help Peso expand its stablecoin payment infrastructure across Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia and Argentina, including services that connect USDT with local currencies through banking and merchant payment systems.

Peso has integrated USDT payments into Yango’s food delivery service in Bolivia, allowing customers to pay for orders using the stablecoin. The fintech offers QR payments, point-of-sale services for merchants and virtual accounts linked to Bolivia’s banking system through ACH transfers. Tether did not disclose the size of its investment.

Source: Tether

The investment comes as other fintech companies expand USDT-based financial services in Bolivia. On Tuesday, lending platform Tala announced a partnership with El Dorado to offer credit directly through the digital wallet, allowing eligible customers to receive and repay loans in USDT on the Tempo blockchain.

Related: Tether, Kazakhstan cenbank mull tenge stablecoin and asset tokenization

Bolivia turns to stablecoins amid US dollar shortage

Bolivia has increasingly turned to stablecoins since 2025 amid a prolonged US dollar shortage and high inflation, with businesses beginning to accept USDT for purchases as access to foreign currency became more difficult.

In November 2025, the government announced plans to integrate cryptocurrencies and stablecoins into the financial system, including allowing banks to offer digital asset custody and crypto-linked financial products.

The government subsequently began considering a regulatory framework in July 2026 that would recognize USDT for payments, savings and trade alongside the boliviano and US dollar.

The proposal came as Bolivia struggled with a prolonged dollar shortage after abandoning its longstanding currency peg in June, fueling demand for dollar-denominated alternatives such as USDT, as Cointelegraph reported in July.

title: Trump didn‘t mention ‘crypto’ once in White House cybercrime roundtable
summary: The US President detailed many schemes defrauding Americans, but referred only to “cybercurrency“ related to scams.
content:
US President Donald Trump hosted a roundtable at the White House on cybercrime, even as he and members of his administration face scrutiny from lawmakers and voters over accusations that they used their positions to enrich themselves with digital assets. 

Speaking at the roundtable event on Wednesday, Trump said “countless” Americans lost more than $20 billion from cybercrime in 2025 through impersonation schemes, ransomware attacks, scam centers and other methods. The president added that federal officials had frozen $1 billion in “cybercurrency tied to foreign scammers” and prevented $1.6 billion in losses in 2025 from going to criminals engaging in cybercrime following a March executive order.

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth (left), President Donald Trump (center) and Attorney General Todd Blanche (right) speaking at the White House on Wednesday. Source: White House

Notably, neither the president nor Attorney General Todd Blanche explicitly used the term “cryptocurrency” or “digital assets” when discussing the scams affecting many Americans, despite reports before the roundtable signaling a crackdown on foreign crypto scams would be the focus of the event. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin similarly only referred to “digital extortion.” “Cybercurrency,” the word Trump used, is a dated term for what many people now call cryptocurrency.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation reported that Americans had lost $11 billion from scams in 2025 specifically related to digital assets, including through crypto ATMs. Cointelegraph reached out to the White House for comment on the roundtable but did not receive an immediate response.

Related: Ex-Trump crypto adviser profited after helping pass stablecoin bill: WSJ

The president and his family are tied to several crypto ventures which Trump reported netted him $1.4 billion in 2025, while his alleged “schemes” cost investors about $4.7 billion, according to a Public Citizen report. His family’s crypto company, World Liberty Financial, also faces scrutiny for its USD1 stablecoin being used to settle a $2 billion investment in Binance by an entity tied to Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan in the United Arab Emirates. 

Trump’s memecoin project, Official Trump (TRUMP), is hosting another dinner for tokenholders on Nov. 22. Similar events organized by the team behind the memecoin have prompted accusations from lawmakers and interest groups of Trump selling access to the presidency through “pay-to-play” schemes.

Italian police arrest 30 people in crypto money laundering scheme

The White House roundtable followed reports that Italian authorities arrested 30 people for using crypto to launder millions of dollars through a bank allegedly tied to the mafia. According to Bloomberg, Italy’s police were investigating a criminal network that sent money from corporate fraud, crypto investment scams, and drug trafficking to digital wallets.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent compared the GENIUS Act’s stablecoin regulations to Abraham Lincoln-era banking reforms, French authorities proposed holding crypto platforms liable for certain DeFi incidents and Elon Musk backed the idea of a Tesla-SpaceX merger that could create a $3.5 trillion technology giant.

Bessent compares GENIUS Act stablecoin rules to Lincoln-era banking reforms

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has compared the newly finalized stablecoin regulations under the GENIUS Act to President Abraham Lincoln’s banking reforms, as the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) prepares to enforce federal rules for stablecoin issuers in January 2027.

In a Wednesday post on X, Bessent described the legislation as a “watershed moment in American finance,” drawing parallels with the National Currency Act of 1863, which created a federal system for nationally chartered banks to issue currency.

Bessent argued that the GENIUS Act could play a similar role in modernizing US payments, strengthening private-sector innovation and reinforcing American leadership in digital assets.

The OCC’s finalized regulations establish requirements for stablecoin reserves, redemptions, risk management and issuer oversight. The framework applies to eligible banks, federally supervised nonbank issuers and certain foreign stablecoin providers.

Starting Jan. 18, 2027, payment stablecoin issuers will generally need appropriate regulatory authorization to operate legally in the United States, with penalties possible for noncompliance.

The regulatory milestone comes as dollar-backed stablecoins gain wider adoption in payments and cross-border transfers, despite slowing growth in their overall circulating supply.

France proposes liability for crypto exchanges offering DeFi access

France wants cryptocurrency platforms to face liability for certain decentralized finance (DeFi) incidents if they fail to vet protocols or ignore known security risks.

French authorities published proposals Wednesday to revise the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA). The joint response to a European Commission consultation came from France’s Treasury, the Financial Markets Authority (AMF), the central bank and the Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR).

“CASPs [crypto-asset service providers] should be liable for certain incidents affecting clients where they actively facilitated access,” French authorities said.

MiCA excludes crypto services provided in a fully decentralized manner without intermediaries. France’s proposal would extend investor safeguards by imposing new duties on regulated platforms that connect customers to DeFi protocols.

The Commission is reviewing whether MiCA needs updating as crypto markets develop. Its consultation sought views on activities outside the law’s original scope, including DeFi. The responses will inform a report to EU lawmakers due by June 30, 2027, which could include proposals to amend the law.

Musk says SpaceX-Tesla merger a ‘good idea’ as AI revenue jumps ninefold 

Elon Musk said he likes the idea of merging Tesla with SpaceX in a potential move that would create a roughly $3.5 trillion technology giant combining AI, space exploration and electric vehicle manufacturing. 

“Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes,” Musk said of the potential merger during a SpaceX Q3 earnings call on Tuesday.

Musk said that both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees of independent directors to discuss the idea at the request of shareholders, though he isn’t able to take part in the discussions due to being a conflicted party.

A merger would bring Tesla into the same corporate group as Grok developer SpaceXAI (formerly xAI) and social media platform X, which SpaceX acquired in February. The talks also come as SpaceX’s AI business became its largest revenue segment in Q3, underscoring how central artificial intelligence has become to Musk’s expanding technology empire.

title: OCC Faces Banking Backlash Over $850 Billion Stablecoin Threat
summary: America’s banking lobby is firing back at federal regulators over a stablecoin rule that could reshape how crypto platforms reward customers. With community bankers warning of an $850 billion lending hit, two powerful banking groups are challenging Washington’s approach to digital dollars. Banking G...
content:
America’s banking lobby is firing back at federal regulators over a stablecoin rule that could reshape how crypto platforms reward customers. With community bankers warning of an $850 billion lending hit, two powerful banking groups are challenging Washington’s approach to digital dollars.

Key Takeaways

  • The ABA blasted the OCC for removing safeguards against indirect stablecoin yield payments.
  • The ICBA told Bitcoin.com News that stablecoin adoption could reduce community bank lending by at least $850 billion.
  • Both banking groups argue crypto rewards could drain deposits and threaten local lending.

Banking Groups Challenge OCC Over Stablecoin Yield Loopholes

The American Bankers Association (ABA) and Independent Community Bankers of America (ICBA) criticized the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) on Wednesday, Oct. 21, over its final rule implementing the GENIUS Act. Both organizations argue that insufficient restrictions on stablecoin rewards could drain deposits from traditional banks, threatening their ability to finance mortgages, small businesses, and local economic activity.

ABA President and CEO Rob Nichols welcomed portions of the framework but sharply criticized the OCC’s decision to abandon previously proposed safeguards against indirect stablecoin yield. “The result is a final rule that will preserve the status quo for crypto platforms despite Congress’s clear intent to protect local lending,” Nichols said in his remarks.

At the heart of the dispute is a rather simple question. If stablecoin issuers cannot directly pay interest, should cryptocurrency exchanges, affiliates, and other business partners be permitted to offer customers similar financial incentives? The ABA argues that these arrangements effectively sidestep Congress’ restrictions.

“The final rule removes the OCC’s originally proposed safeguards that would have addressed indirect arrangements involving affiliates, exchanges and other distribution partners,” Nichols stated. That distinction matters because stablecoins, digital tokens generally designed to maintain a fixed value against currencies such as the U.S. dollar, increasingly compete with conventional financial products.

Community Bankers Warn of $850 Billion Lending Threat

In a note shared with Bitcoin.com News, the ICBA delivered a similarly pointed response, introducing a striking financial estimate into the debate. President and CEO Rebeca Romero Rainey cited the association’s economic analysis, suggesting widespread payment stablecoin adoption could reduce community bank lending by at least $850 billion in the coming years.

That figure represents a projected scenario from the banking association, not an established economic outcome. Romero Rainey emphasized the organization remains concerned about stablecoins operating without sufficient safeguards and meaningful restrictions on interest-like payments.

“We remain focused on ensuring the agency’s policies protect against the risks that payment stablecoins pose to community bank lending, local communities, and financial stability,” she said in a statement shared with our newsdesk.

For community banks, the concern extends beyond competition for customers. Deposits provide the funding that supports loans to farmers, neighborhood businesses, homebuyers and other borrowers who often depend on smaller financial institutions. If customers shift substantial savings into stablecoins offering attractive rewards, community banks could face higher funding costs and tighter lending capacity.

The ICBA has urged regulators to strengthen consumer protections, establish operational limits for stablecoin issuers, and prevent rewards structures from undermining the law’s intended restrictions. Romero Rainey further stressed:

“ICBA will continue working to protect local small businesses, farmers, and consumers from the risks that loosely regulated, yield-bearing payment stablecoins pose to community bank lending capacity.”

A 150-Year-Old Banking Institution Confronts Crypto Competition

The confrontation carries considerable historical weight. Founded in 1875 following the Panic of 1873, the ABA has spent more than 150 years defending the interests of American financial institutions. Its influence extends beyond lobbying. The association helped establish standardized bank routing numbers, advanced check-processing technology, and participated in the creation of the automated clearing house payments network.

Today, it represents an industry safeguarding approximately $20.7 trillion in deposits and extending $13.9 trillion in loans. Interestingly, the ABA isn’t categorically opposed to cryptocurrency or blockchain technology. It insists it supports regulated bank participation in digital asset custody, stablecoin issuance and other blockchain-based financial services.

Its objections center on whether crypto companies should offer deposit-like financial incentives without facing equivalent regulatory obligations. The association has pressed this argument repeatedly, joining 52 state bankers’ associations in December 2025 to demand stronger restrictions on stablecoin rewards. Further appeals continued throughout 2026.

The ABA also opposes a consumer-facing U.S. central bank digital currency, citing concerns about deposit migration and diminished lending capacity. Nichols warned that regulators shouldn’t wait until economic damage materializes before addressing potential deposit losses. The ABA CEO explained:

“Those gaps risk undermining the distinction Congress drew between payment stablecoins and traditional bank deposits.”

For the banking industry, the latest confrontation raises an uncomfortable question. Can traditional lenders compete with digital financial products on their own terms, or will Washington ultimately determine how much competition the stablecoin market is allowed to introduce?

Wednesday, 21/10/2026 | 19:07 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • Helio includes a trading server, administration console, white-label interfaces, and direct liquidity routing.
  • The platform recently integrated with Centroid Solutions for market data and trade execution through FIX.

FX Back Office, a provider of CRM and back-office technology for forex brokers, has integrated Fintake’s Helio trading platform into its technology ecosystem, the companies announced.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Helio has also established connections with other trading technology providers. Its integration with Centroid Solutions allows brokers to use Centroid’s bridge technology for market data and trade execution through the Financial Information eXchange protocol.

Fintake has also confirmed that a connection with TradingView was built and tested for a broker using both platforms. However, the broker’s live launch was not confirmed in earlier reporting.

FXBO Connects Helio to Broker Back Offices

The latest integration connects Helio’s trading infrastructure with FXBO’s customer relationship management and back-office tools. This allows brokers to use the two systems together, according to the announcement.

FXBO CEO Dmitriy Petrenko said the integration would give clients access to Helio alongside the tools they already use.

Helio includes a trading server, an administration console, white-label web and mobile interfaces, and direct liquidity routing. Fintake describes the platform as cloud-native, with an active-active architecture designed to keep multiple environments running at the same time. This setup is intended to support service continuity if one environment experiences a problem.

FXBO and Fintake Plan Further Broker Integrations

The companies said the integration aims to simplify technology deployment for brokers and reduce the work required to connect separate systems. They did not disclose how many brokers are expected to use the integration or identify any existing clients using it.

Fintake founder and CEO Ahmad Said commented that the partnership would allow brokers to deploy Helio under their own brands while connecting it to their back-office systems.

The companies also said they were planning further integrations and joint initiatives. They did not provide details about the planned projects or a timeline for their implementation.

title: Cardano Foundation urges EU against expanding MiCA rules to DeFi and staking
summary: The foundation called for regulation based on financial risks rather than technology, warning that overlapping rules could create uncertainty for crypto businesses across the EU.
content:
The Cardano Foundation has urged the European Union not to introduce new, standalone regulations for decentralized finance and staking, arguing that existing financial laws should govern such activities based on their functions and risks rather than the technologies they use.

In a Wednesday blog post outlining its 19-page Sept. 30 submission to the European Commission, the foundation called for a distinction between direct participation in decentralized networks and financial services provided by intermediaries, particularly those involving custody or control of users’ assets.

“Regulation should follow the substance of an activity, the functions performed, and the risks created, not the technology through which it is conducted,” the foundation wrote.

The foundation said Cardano users can delegate their native ADA (ADA) tokens to help secure the network without surrendering custody or locking their tokens, arguing that such participation should be treated differently from staking services operated by intermediaries.

The submission also called for clearer distinctions between the EU’s Markets in Crypto Assets Regulation (MiCA) and existing financial laws, warning that overlapping requirements and inconsistent interpretations across member states could create uncertainty for crypto businesses.

The foundation’s position comes as EU regulators consider expanding oversight of crypto services. In September, the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) recommended additional safeguards for staking, lending and borrowing, along with a new regulated service category for firms providing access to DeFi protocols.

The Cardano Foundation has also pushed for greater regulatory clarity across the Atlantic, joining five other blockchain organizations in an Oct. 20 letter urging the US Securities and Exchange Commission to formally recognize digital commodities as non-securities under its proposed crypto framework.

title: Broker Websites May Go Offline as Critical PHP Fixes Roll Out
summary:
Brokers with PHP-based websites may temporarily take their public pages offline while applying fixes for two critical security vulnerabilities. Clients won't lose access to their accounts or trading platforms, if they run on separate systems. 
The US National Security Agency warned organisations usi...
content:
2026-10-21T19:42:56.649+02:00

Wednesday, 21/10/2026 | 17:42 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • The NSA advises taking systems offline if they cannot be patched immediately.
  • Brokers have begun warning clients of temporary website outages while assuring them that trading remains available.

Brokers with PHP-based websites may temporarily take their public pages offline while applying fixes for two critical security vulnerabilities. Clients won't lose access to their accounts or trading platforms, if they run on separate systems.

The US National Security Agency warned organisations using PHP to prepare for an urgent update. If they cannot install it immediately, the agency recommended taking affected systems offline until the risk can be addressed.

Effective Immediately, all organizations using PHP for their systems are advised to be prepared for an update addressing two critical vulnerabilities. PHP is widely used for web applications. These vulnerabilities often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database. If an immediate update is not feasible, it is recommend that organizations take the system offline until it can be fully mitigated. NSA will follow up shortly with more specific guidance.

Why Websites May Be Taken Offline

title: Standard Chartered Signs Agreement To Acquire Crypto Custodian Zodia Custody
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Standard Chartered Signs Agreement To Acquire Crypto Custodian Zodia Custody
British bank Standard Chartered will integrate Zodia Custody’s bitcoin and crypto services into its own. 
This post Standard Chartered Signs Agreement To Acquire Crypto Custodian Zodia Custody first appear...
content:
British multinational Standard Chartered will buy digital asset custodian Zodia Custody, months after signing an agreement. 

A statement from London-based Zodia Custody on Wednesday said that the deal will see the company’s service integrated into Standard Chartered’s existing digital asset custody activities. 

Standard Chartered is expanding its crypto-related offerings worldwide. Earlier this month, it said it had plans to offer crypto custody services for institutional clients in Singapore. It already offers the service in the UAE, Luxembourg, and Hong Kong. 

“As institutional adoption of digital assets accelerates, custody is increasingly becoming part of the global banking landscape,” Zodia Custody CEO Richard Clark said. 

He added: “Zodia Custody has built a strong business with the specialist expertise and capabilities to meet the needs of institutional clients. 

“Bringing that expertise together with Standard Chartered’s global reach and established banking platform will strengthen its digital asset custody offering and provide institutions with greater access to trusted, regulated custody services worldwide.”

Ying Ying Tan, global head of securities services and digital assets at Standard Chartered, added that the deal “further deepens our digital asset custody portfolio and reinforces our position as a leading provider of digital asset services globally.”

Zodia Custody shareholders in May approved Standard Chartered’s offer to buy the company. 

The company works to custody bitcoin and other digital assets for institutional and asset managers. 

Standard Chartered has delved deeper into the crypto space in recent years. In 2025, the bank set up a trading desk for bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies in London, making it one of the first global banks to enter spot cryptocurrency trading.

It has since debuted custody and trading services in countries around the world. 

Top banks worldwide are debuting or planning to debut crypto custody services, with State Street, Standard Chartered, U.S. Bank, and Citigroup all committing to direct crypto custody over the past 18 months.

Crypto custody is often a starting point for banks moving into the digital asset space. BNY Mellon in 2022 became the first major U.S. bank to offer digital asset custody services.   

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: UK financial watchdog opens consultations for DeFi guidance, crypto laws
summary: The UK Financial Conduct Authority consultations came just weeks after the agency opened applications for companies under its new crypto regulatory regime.
content:
The UK Financial Conduct Authority consultations came just weeks after the agency opened applications for companies under its new crypto regulatory regime.

The UK’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) announced two consultation periods for how companies using decentralized finance can comply with its guidance, and exclusions for certain crypto assets following “recent legislative changes.”

In a Wednesday notice, the FCA opened consultation periods for helping DeFi companies comply with the financial watchdog’s rules on money laundering and financial crime. The agency also announced a consultation for “exclusions from cryptoasset regulation,” citing recent legislation in the country.

Regarding DeFi, the FCA said that the proposed guidance “seeks to clarify existing rules rather than establish new policy.”

“DeFi sits among the most innovative parts of [Financial Services],” said the UK Cryptoasset Business Council in response to the consultations. “The UK can still strike the right balance - clear perimeter rules, expectations that stay proportionate, and a framework that lets responsible innovation take root here instead of migrating elsewhere [...] the FCA needs to get this right.”

The crypto regulation exclusions referred to the FCA’s reveal of a regulatory regime, including stablecoin holding arrangements and reserve assets, expected to be enforced starting in October 2027. The FCA opened applications for crypto entities on Sept. 30, with a Feb. 28, 2027 deadline for companies seeking to be in compliance with the rules.

title: Treasury Secretary Bessent likens GENIUS Act to Lincoln-era banking reform
summary: The OCC has finalized rules for stablecoin reserves and redemptions, with Bessent calling the GENIUS Act a “watershed moment for American finance.”
content:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has compared the Trump administration’s landmark stablecoin legislation to banking reforms enacted under President Abraham Lincoln, drawing parallels between two efforts to establish a national framework for American currency more than 160 years apart.

In a Wednesday post on X, Bessent hailed the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency’s (OCC) final rule implementing the GENIUS Act, calling the legislation a “watershed moment in American finance.”

Bessent drew a comparison to the National Currency Act of 1863, which established a federal framework for nationally chartered banks to issue currency. He argued that the GENIUS Act serves a similar purpose for payment stablecoins in the digital age.

Bessent said the OCC rule would support “private-sector innovation, competition, and American leadership in digital assets.”

Source: Scott Bessent

As Cointelegraph reported Wednesday, the OCC finalized rules governing stablecoin reserves, redemptions and related services. The rules are scheduled to take effect on Jan. 18, 2027.

Jonathan Gould, comptroller of the currency, described the regulations as a “clear, practical framework for payment stablecoin innovation.”

Related: Mastercard launches stablecoin risk screening for banks and payment providers

What the OCC’s stablecoin rules mean for issuers

The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for payment stablecoins. The OCC’s final rule sets out how that framework will apply to issuers under its supervision, including requirements for reserves, redemptions and risk management.

Beginning Jan. 18, 2027, companies issuing payment stablecoins in the United States will generally need regulatory approval under the GENIUS Act. Issuing stablecoins without the required authorization could carry penalties.

The OCC said the final rule covers national banks, federal savings associations, federal branches of foreign banks and nonbank companies seeking approval to issue payment stablecoins under federal supervision. It also covers certain foreign payment stablecoin issuers.

The rules come as dollar-denominated stablecoins gain traction for payments and money transfers, even as growth in their overall supply has stalled.
