title: Beyond HODLing: How Bitcoin-Backed Loans Can Unlock New Financial Opportunities
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Beyond HODLing: How Bitcoin-Backed Loans Can Unlock New Financial Opportunities
SALT Lending highlights how Bitcoin holders can access liquidity for real estate, business expansion, and other financial opportunities without selling their Bitcoin.
This post Beyond HODLing: How Bitco...
content:
For long-term Bitcoin holders, accessing capital has traditionally presented a difficult choice: sell a portion of their holdings or leave that value untouched.

Bitcoin-backed lending offers another option, allowing holders to borrow against their Bitcoin while maintaining exposure to the asset.

In a recent video shared on X, SALT Lending highlighted how borrowers can use Bitcoin-backed loans for more than simply accessing cash, outlining several ways liquidity can support broader financial goals.

Turning Bitcoin Holdings Into Financial Opportunity

Rather than selling Bitcoin to fund a major purchase or investment, borrowers can pledge their holdings as collateral to access capital while preserving their long-term position.

One potential use case is real estate. Bitcoin holders looking to purchase property may be able to leverage their holdings for liquidity instead of liquidating Bitcoin to fund the transaction.

Business expansion presents another opportunity. Entrepreneurs and business owners can potentially use Bitcoin-backed loans to fund operations, hire employees, or pursue growth opportunities without selling their Bitcoin or giving up equity in their businesses.

SALT Lending also pointed to investment diversification as another possible application. Borrowers may use loan proceeds to access other markets or investment opportunities while retaining exposure to Bitcoin.

Another consideration is tax planning. Selling appreciated Bitcoin can trigger capital gains taxes, while receiving proceeds from a properly structured loan generally does not constitute a taxable sale. However, individual tax circumstances vary, and borrowing introduces additional financial risks.

A Strategic Approach to Bitcoin Liquidity

The broader takeaway from SALT Lending’s video is that Bitcoin-backed borrowing should be viewed as a financial planning decision rather than simply a way to access cash.

Real estate purchases, business investments, and other opportunities all require borrowers to weigh the potential benefits of liquidity against borrowing costs, repayment obligations, and the risks associated with Bitcoin’s price volatility.

Because Bitcoin-backed loans are secured by a volatile asset, significant price declines can increase loan-to-value ratios and potentially require additional collateral or trigger liquidation, depending on the loan terms.

For borrowers with a clear financial strategy, however, the ability to access capital without immediately selling Bitcoin creates another avenue for putting their holdings to use.

SALT Lending provides Bitcoin-backed lending solutions designed to help eligible borrowers access liquidity while maintaining their long-term Bitcoin exposure.

As Bitcoin continues to evolve beyond an asset primarily associated with buying and holding, lending may play an increasingly important role in how holders manage their finances and pursue opportunities without necessarily selling their Bitcoin.

title: Trump to throw spotlight on overseas crypto abuses at White House event
summary: The president is hosting a cybercrime event that will highlight U.S. authorities' efforts to crack down on crypto scams run by foreign criminal organizations.
content:
Summary

  • At a White House cybercrime event, President Donald Trump is set to highlight how much his administration has done to pursue overseas crypto criminals.
  • Under his watch, U.S. law enforcement has halted about $833 million in fraudulent crypto transactions, an official said.

President Donald Trump planned to put special focus on his administration's efforts against overseas crypto-fueled criminal operations at a Wednesday event on cybercrime, according to a White House official.

Crypto-related scams have stolen tens of billions from U.S. citizens, and Trump was set to highlight how much his administration is targeting and disrupting the transnational organizations behind it. Multinational criminal cartels have set up elaborate scam centers designed to steal money through relationship scams, phishing campaigns, ransomware attacks and other fraudulent means, and the official said that the U.S. strategies to seize funds and shut down the operations will be discussed.

The administration says its law enforcement agencies have halted about $833 million in crypto connected to the overseas scams, and 503 fraudulent crypto websites have been seized under the watch of the Homeland Security Task Force. It's also informed almost 9,000 U.S. citizens that they're being victimized, the official said.

In November, the Department of the Treasury announced it had formed a multi-agency Scam Center Strike Force that pursued so-called "pig butchering" that was coordinated by widespread and well-funded organized-crime operations in places such as Burma, Cambodia, Laos and the Philippines.

Since last year, the U.S. issued a number of sanctions to meant to wall off the websites and infrastructure behind such attacks.

On the home front, though, Trump's personal crypto ties may have become a political liability. As the congressional midterm elections approach in a couple of weeks, digital assets have taken up a prominent role in self-dealing accusations levied against the president and his administration.

summary:

supported orders without approving each trade individually.
London's trading industry is coming home!
The move follows the
b...

2026-10-21T18:14:13.277+02:00

Wednesday, 21/10/2026 | 16:14 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • Autonomous Trading covers more than 75,000 listed stocks, options and ETFs worldwide.
  • The firm connects ChatGPT, Claude, Grok and Perplexity through the Model Context Protocol.

Interactive Brokers has introduced a feature that allows eligible clients to authorise connected artificial intelligence platforms to identify trading opportunities and submit supported orders without approving each trade individually.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The move follows the broker's earlier expansion of AI integrations. In June, Interactive Brokers introduced an integration with Claude that allowed clients to analyse portfolios and generate trading instructions for review. It later expanded its connections to ChatGPT, Grok and other AI tools. Autonomous Trading adds the option for these systems to submit orders on clients' behalf.

Interactive Brokers Adds Autonomous AI Trading

Called IBKR Autonomous Trading, the feature covers more than 75,000 listed stocks, options and exchange-traded funds worldwide. Clients can define trading instructions in natural language and set the conditions under which connected AI systems can act.

The feature operates through a dedicated AI Partition within an existing account. Clients can fund it by transferring money from their main account, without opening a separate account or making an external deposit.

Interactive Brokers said the AI operates within client-defined instructions, subject to account restrictions and safeguards designed to help manage risk.

Milan Galik, Chief Executive Officer of Interactive Brokers, said the feature builds on the company's use of automation .

“IBKR Autonomous Trading builds on that approach, allowing clients to define their trading strategies and safeguards while connected AI monitors markets and executes trades within those parameters,” Galik said.

AI Trading Includes Volatility and Portfolio Rules

Clients can set conditions for monitoring implied volatility , reviewing positions that fall below a specified price level, or reducing holdings that exceed portfolio allocation limits.

They can also instruct the AI to sell 30-day covered calls when a holding's implied volatility reaches the 90th percentile of its range over the previous 52 weeks. All actions remain subject to supported order types and account restrictions.

Interactive Brokers' existing AI Integration connects accounts to platforms including ChatGPT, Claude, Grok and Perplexity through the Model Context Protocol, without sharing API keys or passwords.

The broker also offers AI Screeners, Investment Themes and Connections tools. Access to Autonomous Trading depends on country, regulatory and account eligibility, and is subject to funding and other limits that may change over time.

title: Kalshi Pushes Deeper Into Crypto Derivatives With Bitcoin-Backed Margin Loans
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Kalshi Pushes Deeper Into Crypto Derivatives With Bitcoin-Backed Margin Loans
A new tri-party lending structure with BitGo lets Kalshi Prime clients borrow against bitcoin to margin perpetual futures.
This post Kalshi Pushes Deeper Into Crypto Derivatives With Bitcoin-Backed Margin...
content:
Kalshi is doubling down on its bid to become the regulated U.S. home for crypto perpetual futures, pairing a new bitcoin-backed lending arrangement with digital-asset custodian BitGo alongside a distribution deal that will put its perpetual contracts in front of Webull’s more than 6 million customers.

Bloomberg first reported Wednesday that customers of Kalshi Prime, the company’s U.S.-registered futures commission merchant, will be able to borrow against digital assets held at BitGo and use the proceeds to fund margin positions on perpetual futures traded on Kalshi’s main exchange. 

Under the tri-party structure, loans will be issued by Kalshi Katalyst, a lending affiliate of Kalshi Prime, and secured against assets held at BitGo Bank & Trust, the firm’s federally chartered trust bank.

Eligible collateral will include bitcoin, ethereum and stablecoins deemed compliant with the GENIUS Act, with additional custodians expected to join Kalshi’s network over time. 

Prime CEO Jeff Bandman told the outlet the product was designed with crypto-native traders in mind, including those already active on unregulated offshore perpetuals venues and large holders who would rather not sell their bitcoin to fund futures positions. 

He also pointed to unexpected demand from businesses, such as Latin American firms that run their operations on U.S. dollar stablecoins.

The move targets a segment where the company has acknowledged a structural disadvantage against Polymarket, its offshore, blockchain-based rival, which has long catered to crypto whales and trading firms that prefer to keep their capital in digital assets. The two platforms have been racing to build out perpetuals since the spring.

Webull debuting crypto-linked perpetual futures via Kalshi rails

The BitGo arrangement landed a day after Webull announced Tuesday that eligible U.S. customers will be able to trade perpetual futures on its platform beginning in November, starting with bitcoin and a handful of other crypto assets. 

The contracts will trade on KalshiEX LLC, Kalshi’s CFTC-regulated designated contract market, and clear through Kalshi Klear LLC, its derivatives clearing organization. Access will initially be limited to customers already approved for futures trading through existing Webull Futures accounts, with broader availability expected before year-end.

Webull Group President and U.S. CEO Anthony Denier said in the company’s release that perpetual futures saw more than $90 trillion in global volume in 2025 and that American investors should be able to access them through a regulated platform. 

These two announcements extend a product buildout for the company, which secured CFTC clearance for the first U.S.-regulated bitcoin perpetual in late May and went live with the contract in early June, before adding gold and silver perpetuals in September and a US500 stock index perpetual earlier this month. 

The expansion comes amid mounting state-level legal pressure, with Utah becoming the latest state to sue Kalshi on Monday over what it alleges is illegal sports gambling, following New York’s similar action against Polymarket last month.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

Bitcoin Nears $85,000 as SpaceX Earnings Reignite Risk Appetite
The price of bitcoin is rising fast — with the stock market — as investors feel bullish on tech.

content:
Bitcoin’s price rose above $84,500 on Wednesday as investors flooded back into risk-on assets — particularly tech-related stocks. 

The leading cryptocurrency was recently priced at $84,461 after rising nearly as high as $84,588 earlier on Wednesday morning in New York. 

Over a 24-hour period, the coin is up 2%. Zooming out over a seven-day timeframe and it is up 3%. 

Bitcoin’s rise comes as SpaceX reported surging revenue growth in its third quarter, and its owner, Elon Musk, talked of a potential SpaceX-Tesla merger.

SpaceX — which debuted in June on the Nasdaq in the biggest initial public offering ever — reported third-quarter revenue on Tuesday of $14.6 billion, up 161% from the previous year and smashing estimates. 

Technology stocks rallied on the news. Bitcoin has in the past risen with risk assets and been correlated with the Nasdaq. 

But this year, the OG cryptocurrency has moved with gold as the so-called debasement trade becomes hot again. The trade is when investors buy certain assets to hedge against currency being devalued. 

The dollar slid in value in August after the U.S. Treasury Department said it would more than double the size of its government debt repurchases. Bitcoin had its best quarterly run in three years and third best August ever.   

U.S. investors this week have piled back into spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds, too. On Monday and Tuesday, the funds managed by BlackRock, Fidelity, Grayscale, and others received new investment of over $549 million, according to Coinglass data. 

Bitcoin’s price is still over 30% below its all-time high of $126,080 — reached in October 2025 — but analysts are saying the cryptocurrency is now back in a bull market after spending most of this year in a bear. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: How a16z-backed DATA is rethinking its blockchain strategy after $30 million Sui deal
summary: The startup is retiring its own blockchain and moving to Sui with a $30 million investment as it narrows its focus to AI training data.
content:
Updated Oct 21, 2026, 11:24 a.m. EDTPublished Oct 21, 2026, 11:22 a.m. EDT

4 min read

Summary

  • DATA shifted from its broad intellectual property ambitions to AI training data after finding that established licensing markets were difficult to disrupt, CEO Andrea Muttoni told CoinDesk.
  • The startup is moving to Sui following a $30 million investment from Sui Foundation, allowing the company to focus on its data verification tools rather than maintaining its own blockchain.
  • DATA's Trace registry tracks the origins, consent terms and licensing history of AI training data, with partner Kled adding millions of contributions each day.

DATA, the blockchain startup backed by Andreessen Horowitz's a16z crypto and formerly known as Story Protocol, is shutting down its blockchain and moving to Sui after securing a $30 million investment from the network's foundation.

The move comes after spending years trying to bring intellectual property onchain. But after raising $140 million and building its own blockchain, the company found that changing how the world's intellectual property is licensed was harder than expected.

"We were trying to boil the ocean, and it was a very saturated and entrenched ocean," Andrea Muttoni, CEO of DATA Foundation, told CoinDesk in an interview.

That realization helped drive Story’s rebrand to DATA Foundation in June, when it shifted its attention to the market for AI training data. Four months later, the company is now narrowing its focus further to tracking the origins and usage rights of data used to train artificial intelligence models.

When the Bellevue, Washington-based startup was founded in 2022, the original plan covered everything from music royalties to patents and trademarks. The idea was to let owners register their intellectual property on a blockchain and set terms for how others could use it. The problem, Muttoni said, was that many of those industries already had systems in place, while large rights holders had little interest in making their intellectual property available for permissionless licensing.

"We were kind of spreading ourselves way too thin across so many different types of IP," he said.

Then came the rebrand earlier this year.

However, after that, the team began to question whether it still needed to maintain an entire blockchain, given that most of its work centered on a single product: Trace, which is a registry that records where training data comes from, who contributed it and what rights buyers have to use it.

Also, running a blockchain comes with costs, including engineers, validators, audits and infrastructure providers.

"Does it still make sense to run our own L1, or should we focus most of our energy on the protocol, on the product, on Trace?" he said.

That line of thinking led to the decision to shut down its blockchain and move to Sui.

Muttoni did not disclose how much of Story's original $140 million in funding remains, but said its existing investors, including a16z crypto, are still involved.

Now, Muttoni is positioning the new focus as a continuation of the first rebrand rather than another change in direction.

Finding a market in AI data

The company's new strategy grew partly out of its experience with Poseidon, an AI data company incubated by the Story team that collects and processes data for training AI models.

Muttoni said the team found a market where buyers often had little way to check whether the datasets they were purchasing were original, properly licensed or even exclusive. In one case, vendors offered Poseidon supposedly exclusive datasets that were already available from other sellers.

"We were at one point given our own data set back to us," he said.

DATA is trying to address that problem through its product, Trace.

For example, when someone uploads a video or voice recording via a participating data marketplace, Trace creates a receipt for that file. The record includes details such as when it was submitted, the terms the contributor agreed to and any later licensing or payment events.

Kled, a marketplace that pays people to contribute data, accounts for much of the activity. Muttoni said the platform is adding between 3 million and 4 million contributions a day, including older records being brought onto Trace.

The figures show how much data is being registered, though not necessarily how much has been sold. DATA did not disclose how many records have generated licensing revenue.

The move comes as more crypto projects shift toward AI, betting on growing demand for training data and tools to track its origins. Muttoni estimates the AI training data market could be worth hundreds of billions of dollars.

For now, Muttoni said, the goal is not to compete with data marketplaces but to provide a record that buyers and sellers can check. "The main goal for now is being the infrastructure for, let's say, the auditability and provenance of data," he said.

He didn't rule out DATA eventually operating its own marketplace, but didn’t provide any further details.

Why Sui?

Moving to Sui means DATA will no longer need to run its own blockchain, while gaining access to tools that Muttoni said fit what the company wants to build next.

One is Walrus, a decentralized storage platform that can hold copies of the original files registered through Trace. Another is Seal, which can encrypt those files and restrict access to buyers with the right permissions.

Today, Trace records information about a file rather than storing the file itself. Adding storage would let buyers compare what they receive with the original submission, making it easier to spot changes.

Sui Foundation will become DATA Network's largest institutional holder through its $30 million investment. Muttoni said Sui is taking a hands-off approach to DATA's product plans. Financial details weren’t disclosed.

The company also plans to move its existing token to Sui on a one-to-one basis, with its current blockchain remaining operational until the migration is complete. Existing $DATA tokens will move to Sui one-to-one, with holders retaining their rights and vesting schedules unchanged, according to a press release.

For Muttoni, the decision comes down to concentrating on the part of DATA’s original business that attracted the most interest.

"We were thinking of going in one direction, but you see the wind keeps pulling you in a different direction," he said. "Maybe the wind is coming from that way."

title: Bybit will look for big broker partnerships to take on Robinhood in the U.S.
summary: When it comes to the U.S., Bybit will look to work with with someone like Interactive Brokers (IB), for example, said CEO Ben Zhou.
content:
Updated Oct 21, 2026, 11:30 a.m. EDTPublished Oct 21, 2026, 11:09 a.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • Bybit CEO Ben Zhou said partnerships are a standard approach of Bybit’s when entering new territories.
  • The second-largest cryptocurrency exchange is looking to expand into the U.K., saying it remains an attractive, untapped market.

Bybit, the second-largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume, plans to buddy up with an established local company when it enters the U.S. to help it challenge the reach of firms like Robinhood Markets HOOD$101.93·Market Closed, according to CEO Ben Zhou.

Zhou said finding a partner is Bybit’s standard approach when entering new territories, suggesting that for the U.S., Bybit will consider working with a company such as Interactive Brokers (IB), for example.

“It’s best at this stage to work with a partner who wants to enter the crypto field and who already has a client base in the U.S.,” Zhou said in an interview. “For example, IB or one of those guys who haven't gone into crypto and have a good U.S. base.”

Bybit, which has in excess of 80 million registered users worldwide across more than 180 countries and regions, has been collecting licenses globally with a view to offering a range of new regulated products. In Europe, for example, it plans to deploy an everything app offering derivatives and tokenized stocks as early as the first quarter of next year.

Bybit’s partnership approach cuts out the onerous alternative, taken by the likes of Coinbase Global COIN$177.07·Market Closed, to cross the U.S. state by state gathering money transfer licenses, culminating in a coveted New York state Bit License.

The state-by-state licensing process would take two to three years, Zhou said. “I might as well just wait for [the] Clarity [Act] to pass or have a better understanding of what the new law is. Maybe the SEC is going to take over, and then it's going to be one regulator, one license, and everything is covered at the federal level.”

The fact that Bybit has not yet attempted to establish a presence in the world’s largest economy is to its advantage, Zhou said.

“Bybit is the only one that's been sitting out of the U.S., and as a result we have a completely clear record there,” he said. “So we can actually go in any time if the moment is right. I think I should use that good record to our advantage and wait for the best moment to enter, rather than rush to FOMO in.”

FOMO, or fear of missing out, can steer people or companies to act in an unconsidered manner that may end up to their detriment.

While the U.S. is a big and hugely important market, it's also highly competitive and very saturated, Zhou said, with the established stature of firms like Coinbase, and the growing importance of Robinhood.

So where in the world does Bybit think is good for growth?

Even Southeast Asia, Latin America, Africa are all pretty competitive, Zhou said. One place where competition is not so concentrated and which remains a “pretty good market,” is the U.K., according to Zhou.

“The U.K. is looking towards a new regime for crypto, and none of the global exchanges are dominant there,” Zhou said. “The main player is probably Coinbase. So from a preliminary look, it seems like a very untapped market. But again, the cost to enter is very high and would almost take the same effort as a MiCA license in the EU. But we're looking into it.”

Early this year, Zhou was invited to meet government-linked bodies including the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and members of the House of Lords, the parliament’s upper chamber.

Asked if Bybit has a London office, Zhou said: “We're looking, but we haven't decided where yet.”

title: Crypto Long & Short: Why real-world assets need fixed-rate loans onchain
summary: Real-world assets already back the largest stablecoins, yet borrowing against them onchain still runs through variable-rate pools. Peter Gaffney of O2O Capital Partners explains why fixed-rate, fixed-term lending is the missing piece, and how a 5% shift in Sky and Ethena reserves could create $1.8 b...
content:
Oct 21, 2026, 11:00 a.m. EDT

5 min read

Summary

You're reading Crypto Long & Short, our weekly newsletter featuring insights, news and analysis for the professional investor. Sign up here to get it in your inbox every Wednesday.

Fixed-rate lending is the clearest growth lever for real-world assets (RWAs) in decentralized finance (DeFi). It unlocks a strategy that credit desks have run for decades but DeFi has never meaningfully implemented: buy a quality income asset, borrow against it at a locked rate below the asset’s yield and buy more of the asset. Stablecoins are steadily sitting around $300 billion in supply and aggregate vault assets are nearing the $20 billion milestone. Morpho alone carries more than $16 billion in deposits, most of it in variable-rate markets priced on pool utilization, which serve crypto-native traders who manage liquid positions in real time but leave longer-dated borrowers with uncertainty. Fixed-rate, fixed-term lending closes that gap by matching the term of the loan to the duration of the collateral, especially for RWAs whose redemptions can settle anywhere from T+7 to T+90. With the borrow cost and maturity known at entry, institutional counterparties can underwrite an RWA looping vault the same way they approve conventional term financing. This is the same bedrock foundation that formed and grew traditional credit markets to $51 trillion in US fixed income versus $1.6 trillion in floating-rate leveraged loans. The move to fixed rates is already underway: Morpho recently opened fixed-rate, fixed-term markets through Morpho Midnight, which Coinbase used to launch fixed-rate crypto-backed loans to its customers in September 2026.

DeFi is a battle-tested real-time execution engine with a narrow collateral base of volatile crypto assets that move by magnitudes in stress. This is what turned the October 10, 2025 liquidation cascade into a $19 billion event, marking the start of a nearly 60% reduction in DeFi total value locked for the eight months to follow. Expanding DeFi beyond crypto requires non-crypto-correlated RWAs, and RWAs require more precise lending markets to scale. RWAs already back the largest stablecoins, with Ethena and Sky committing more than $2.4 billion to JAAA, BUIDL, STAC, and USTB.

RWA leverage onchain runs almost entirely through variable-rate pools, where the borrow rate is set by utilization rather than by a lender agreeing to a price. Illustratively, Aave’s rate curve lifts the USDC borrow rate from 4% to 14% as utilization climbs from 92% to 100%. JAAA yields between 4.5% and 5% and Maple’s syrupUSDC pays 5.2%, while the one-year average USDC borrow rate on Aave V3 Ethereum is 4.56%, leaving just 50 basis points of spread to work with. The variance in these borrow rates scares off would-be RWA loopers or limits them to double-digit-yielding RWAs, which greatly narrows the accessible universe of investment-grade credit. Coin Metrics found routine daily utilization spikes on a $2 billion pool and the April 2026 KelpDAO rsETH exploit pinned Aave’s USDC pool at 100% utilization, causing borrowers to pay the maximum 14% rate for five days. Since tokenized credit products can take anywhere from T+1 to well beyond T+90 to settle redemptions, a spike like that can outlast the holder’s ability to exit while running an unprofitable trade.

Fixed-rate, fixed-term lending solves this because it lets the allocator match the duration of the loan to the duration of the RWA, the same way a bank extends a 70% advance at a fixed spread against investment-grade paper. Fixed-rate platforms like Tenor Finance, Kamino, Term Labs and Loopscale now quote rates against products, with a Kamino market offering 5.3% fixed-rate loans against Figure’s auto loan portfolio in rolling 30-day terms. Combined with one-click leverage providers, which compress multiple loops into a single transaction, these markets let institutional underwriters size into leveraged RWA positions at scale.

For sizing, a 5% reallocation of the $12 billion in Sky and Ethena reserve capital into fixed-rate looped RWA strategies at 3x is $600 million of equity and $1.8 billion of RWA demand, before foundations, digital asset treasury companies and exchange Earn programs contribute to growth. Well-positioned issuers of underwritten, loopable, non-crypto correlated RWAs will be the beneficiaries as DeFi’s collateral base finally grows beyond crypto.

Headlines of the week

by Francisco Rodrigues

This week’s headlines show banks further expanding blockchain payments and crypto services, while MSCI tightened index eligibility and BlackRock proposed a new way for its clients to manage bitcoin exposure.

  • JPMorgan brings tokenized dollar deposits to Ethereum: The bank deployed JPM Coin on Ethereum for institutional clients, expanding beyond Base and allowing customers to use tokenized bank deposits for blockchain payments and settlement.
  • Thirty-seven-bank euro stablecoin venture secures Dutch e-money license: Qivalis, backed by banks including BNP Paribas, ING and BBVA, received authorization as an electronic money institution but must complete remaining requirements under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation before issuing its planned euro token.
  • MSCI adopts rules that could remove Strategy and Metaplanet from equity indexes: New financial screens will exclude companies classified as non-operating, with affected constituents to be announced Nov. 11 and changes effective after the Nov. 30 close; neither company’s removal is yet confirmed.
  • Kraken parent Payward agrees to buy Lithuania’s Saldo Bank: The acquisition would expand Payward’s European business into interest-bearing deposits, lending, card issuance and euro payments, with closing expected in 2027 subject to regulatory approvals.
  • BlackRock files for a bitcoin ETF designed to cushion losses: The proposed iShares Bitcoin Managed Protection ETF (PBIT) would use options linked to the iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) to seek downside protection in exchange for limited upside, without guaranteeing investors a fixed loss limit.

Tron was the largest chain for crypto card volume in the third quarter of 2026 with a 27.5% share (about $638 million). The weekly share has since fallen to 23.7%, as total card volume grew and Tron’s volume held steady. Tron’s TRX has been roughly flat at $0.33 to $0.34.

title: The CPA Arms Race: How Can Brokers Compete Without Running Permanent Losses?
summary:
The CPA model has long been one of the most direct ways for
brokers to acquire clients and introducer books. It is simple, trackable, and
commercially clear: pay a fixed amount for a qualified client, then aim to
recover that cost through spreads, commissions, and lifetime value. In theory,
this ali...
content:
2026-10-21T17:00:00.000+02:00

Wednesday, 21/10/2026 | 15:00 GMT by Anish Lal

  • Anish Lal, Chief Business Development Officer at BlackBull Markets, highlights how faster reporting, reliable monthly payments and dedicated support can help brokers attract introducers without matching the highest CPA rates.
  • Brokers tolerating CPA abuse may struggle as competition increases and client quality declines.

The CPA model has long been one of the most direct ways for brokers to acquire clients and introducer books. It is simple, trackable, and commercially clear: pay a fixed amount for a qualified client, then aim to recover that cost through spreads, commissions, and lifetime value. In theory, this aligns interests. In practice, the model is under increasing strain.

London's trading industry is coming home!

CPA Costs and Acquisition Losses

In many markets, advertised or privately negotiated CPAs now routinely exceed the average initial deposit. A broker may pay an $800 CPA for a client whose average first deposit is $400–$500, accepting an immediate loss on the assumption that the client will deposit again and generate enough activity over 6–12 months to recover the cost.

If that client churns after one or two months, the acquisition is loss-making.

Some brokers are prepared to run these early losses as a deliberate strategy to lock in introducers and build scale. Others go further, showing a longer tolerance for CPA abuse, such as multiple accounts, self-referrals, or low-quality traffic, because they prioritise volume or believe the economics still work at portfolio level. This raises a straightforward question: where is the sustainable value?

Client Quality and Introducer Retention

Two introducers can deliver similar volumes yet produce very different outcomes. One sends clients who deposit $1,000 on average and remain active for 8–10 months; the other sends clients who deposit $300 and largely disappear within 60 days.

Even if both are paid the same CPA, the first book is far more valuable. Brokers that can identify and retain higher-quality introducers create residual value. Those that compete only on the headline CPA rate often end up paying the same amount for markedly weaker economics.

Some firms accept a longer tolerance for abuse because they need the volume to support other commercial goals or have the balance sheet to absorb a higher proportion of short-lived clients. That approach can succeed for a time. It becomes harder to sustain once competitors match the rates and the quality of the books being acquired begins to decline.

At that point, the advantage shifts to brokers that can show introducers something other than the highest possible CPA. A broker that does not match the top market CPA can still win an introducer’s preference by offering faster and more transparent reporting, reliable monthly payments , dedicated support, and a platform that clients do not leave.

Managing CPA Costs and Long-Term Value

The introducer accepts a lower headline CPA because the overall commercial relationship and client retention are stronger. Over time, that broker retains more of the value created by the book. Competing on pure CPA alone is increasingly difficult. The more durable approach is to treat the CPA as one component of a broader commercial relationship rather than the sole lever.

Brokers that invest in the quality of the client experience, maintain disciplined filters on traffic, and are willing to walk away from books that only work at unsustainable acquisition costs tend to keep more of the value they create.

Those that rely primarily on outbidding others for volume often find that the books they acquire become less valuable over time, even as the cost of acquiring them continues to rise. The CPA model is not broken.

It remains one of the cleanest ways to reward introducers for performance. But the firms that extract lasting value from it are those that treat it as a measured commercial tool rather than an open-ended arms race.

In a market where many are prepared to run losses to secure books, the competitive edge increasingly belongs to those who know which losses are worth taking and which are not.

title: Bitcoin Price Prediction: Michael Saylor Says BTC Will Reach $100K in 12 Months as 4-Year Bull Run Begins
summary: Bitcoin price prediction discussions have gained fresh attention after Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor forecast that BTC could return to $100,000 within the next 12 months.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin price prediction discussions have gained fresh attention after Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor forecast that BTC could return to $100,000 within the next 12 months.

Speaking on the Schwab Network, Saylor said the cryptocurrency was entering a new bull market and predicted that the broader rally could last four years. His outlook comes as Bitcoin trades near $83,700, with technical indicators showing a positive trend but mixed short-term momentum.

Saylor’s forecast reflects his long-standing confidence in Bitcoin’s limited supply and its potential role in financial markets. However, the $100,000 target remains a projection rather than a confirmed outcome. Monetary policy, institutional demand, regulatory developments, and market liquidity could all influence the cryptocurrency’s next move.

Key Facts

  • Bitcoin price prediction: Saylor expects BTC to return above $100,000 within the next 12 months but did not guarantee that the target would be reached by the end of 2026.
  • Four-year bull market: The Strategy executive chairman described the current phase as the beginning of a bull run that could last four years.
  • Current BTC price: Bitcoin was trading around $83,700 in the supplied market snapshot, leaving it approximately 19.4% below $100,000.
  • Strategy’s Bitcoin holdings: The company reported holdings of 848,517 BTC, alongside approximately $5.2 billion in cash reserves, according to the supplied source report.
  • Technical outlook: TradingView’s technical summary indicated a Buy rating, supported by moving averages, while oscillators remained broadly neutral.
  • Corporate strategy: Strategy is pursuing a proposal for daily dividend payments on its credit instruments, with a shareholder vote scheduled for October 28.

Bitcoin Clears Its 200-Week Average as Headwinds Fade

Saylor said Bitcoin had rebounded from its 200-week moving average and climbed approximately $20,000 above that level. He views the recovery as evidence that the previous downturn has run its course and that the market may be entering a new expansion phase.

“I feel like we’re at the beginning of a bull run,” Saylor told the Schwab Network. He also said he expected Bitcoin to return to six-figure valuations within 12 months, while acknowledging that he could not be certain it would happen before the end of 2026. When asked how long the bull market might last, he replied, “Four years.”

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The forecast comes as Bitcoin remains below its October 2025 all-time high of approximately $126,198, according to the supplied market report. At around $83,700, BTC would need to gain roughly 19.4% to reclaim $100,000. A move to that level would represent a meaningful recovery, although it would not establish a new record.

Saylor attributed recent market pressure to restrictive monetary, foreign, and trade policies, alongside competition for investment capital from artificial intelligence. He argued that these forces had weighed on Bitcoin without necessarily undermining its underlying investment case.

He also pointed to the potential expansion of Bitcoin-backed lending, regulatory guidance from US financial authorities, and the development of tokenized securities as factors that could support wider adoption. These developments could improve access to digital assets, although their effect on Bitcoin’s price will depend on actual demand and market conditions.

Bitcoin Price Prediction: What Technical Indicators Show

The TradingView snapshot placed BTC near $83,729, with the overall technical assessment at Buy. Moving averages were classified as Strong Buy, while oscillators remained Neutral. This combination suggests that the prevailing trend is constructive, but short-term momentum has not confirmed a strong breakout.

A close above $83,600 could push the price toward $84,000, while a drop below $83,300 may trigger a pullback toward the $82,950 point of control (POC). Source: kenkemdayfx on TradingView

Bitcoin was trading above several short- and medium-term moving averages, including the 10-period exponential moving average near $82,519 and the 20-period exponential moving average around $82,613. The 50-period EMA stood near $80,733, while the 200-period EMA was approximately $76,071. These levels provide reference points for assessing whether the recent recovery remains intact.

The relative strength index was around 54, a neutral reading that does not indicate an overbought market. The Average Directional Index was near 19, suggesting limited trend strength. Together, these indicators point to a market with a positive moving-average structure but without decisive confirmation of accelerating momentum.

Key price levels also offer a framework for monitoring the BTC price. The $82,000–$83,000 area forms an important near-term support zone, while resistance begins around $84,700 and extends toward $89,000. A sustained move above this resistance region could strengthen the case for a continued recovery. Conversely, a breakdown below the support cluster could expose lower levels, including the mid-$70,000 range.

Saylor Calls the CLARITY Act a Bill of Restrictions

Saylor also discussed the stalled CLARITY Act, a proposed US legislative framework for digital assets. He argued that the legislation placed excessive emphasis on restrictions rather than establishing clear permissions for innovation.

“If you want to create a great economy or a great nation, what you want is a bill of rights, not a bill of restrictions,” Saylor said during the interview. He criticized the proposal’s length and argued that its provisions would have imposed substantial constraints on the digital asset industry.

Michael Saylor argues that the CLARITY Act’s potential failure could benefit Bitcoin by reducing regulatory uncertainty and allowing the market to develop in ways that support a stronger bull run. Source: @AltcoinDaily via X

Instead, Saylor pointed to guidance and initiatives involving the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, and the US Treasury. He said developments involving tokenization, digital derivatives, and digital currency issuance could provide a more favorable environment for financial innovation.

Regulatory clarity can influence institutional participation by helping businesses understand the rules governing custody, trading, issuance, and other digital asset activities. However, the precise effects on Bitcoin demand will depend on how policies are implemented and whether they encourage additional investment.

Saylor also emphasized monetary policy as a central influence on financial markets. Lower borrowing costs and improved liquidity can support demand for risk assets, while restrictive financial conditions may limit investment. Bitcoin remains sensitive to these shifts, despite its fixed maximum supply of 21 million coins.

The distinction matters for the current Bitcoin price prediction. A more supportive regulatory environment may encourage participation, but it cannot guarantee a sustained rally if liquidity tightens or investors reduce exposure to volatile assets.

Strategy’s 845,000 Bitcoin and the Oct. 28 Dividend Vote

Strategy’s substantial Bitcoin holdings remain central to Saylor’s long-term outlook. The company’s reported position of 848,517 BTC, valued at roughly $70 billion at the prices cited in the source report, makes it one of the largest corporate holders of the cryptocurrency. Its cash reserves of approximately $5.2 billion provide additional financial resources as the company manages its capital structure.

Saylor said Strategy had acquired approximately 160,000 BTC during 2026, describing the company as the world’s largest Bitcoin buyer. Its approach, however, extends beyond simply accumulating and holding the asset. Strategy also manages equity and credit instruments to support its financing activities and maintain access to capital.

That approach is particularly relevant to the company’s preferred securities, including STRC. These instruments form part of Strategy’s digital credit strategy, which Saylor views as an important component of its broader business model. Their performance and liquidity can influence financing costs and the company’s ability to continue acquiring Bitcoin.

Shareholders are scheduled to vote on October 28 on a proposal to move dividend payments on certain credit instruments to a daily calendar-day schedule. Saylor said the proposed securities would be the first in the world to pay dividends every calendar day. The plan is intended to align payments more closely with digital markets that operate around the clock, including weekends and holidays.

Daily distributions could change how investors manage cash flows and trade these securities. However, the proposal’s approval, implementation, and eventual effect on trading behavior remain important considerations.

Strategy’s financial structure also creates exposure to Bitcoin’s volatility. A rising BTC price can increase the value of its holdings, while a prolonged decline can pressure the company’s market valuation and financing conditions. Its cash reserves and capital-management policies therefore matter alongside the size of its Bitcoin position.

Institutional Forecasts Add Context to Bitcoin’s Long-Term Outlook

Saylor’s bullish outlook comes as traditional financial institutions increasingly examine Bitcoin’s potential role in investment portfolios. J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions report, released on October 19, introduced a range of long-term return expectations for Bitcoin. The report assesses asset classes over a 10- to 15-year horizon rather than attempting to predict short-term price movements.

Michael Saylor cites J.P. Morgan’s 10-year forecast, which projects Bitcoin’s 10% annualized return to outperform REITs, stocks, bonds, gold, and cash. Source: Michael Saylor via X

This distinction is important when evaluating Bitcoin predictions. Long-term portfolio assumptions do not establish where BTC will trade over the next 12 months, and they should not be interpreted as confirmation of Saylor’s $100,000 target.

Bitcoin’s limited supply remains central to the investment argument advanced by Saylor. He has argued that artificial intelligence may generate substantial corporate wealth but cannot increase Bitcoin’s predetermined supply. In his view, that scarcity distinguishes BTC from assets whose supply can expand through additional production or issuance.

Even so, scarcity alone does not determine market value. Investor demand, liquidity, regulation, and broader economic conditions remain significant influences on the price of Bitcoin. Institutional participation can support demand, but it can also change as portfolio managers reassess risk.

BTC Price Prediction: Can Bitcoin Reach $100K Within 12 Months?

Bitcoin’s near-term outlook combines a constructive moving-average structure with resistance that the market must overcome. At approximately $83,700, the cryptocurrency needs a gain of about 19.4% to reach $100,000. That move is possible, but the technical indicators supplied do not establish that it will occur within Saylor’s proposed timeframe.

A sustained move above the $84,700–$89,000 resistance area would provide stronger evidence of improving momentum. Beyond that range, traders would monitor whether buying activity remains sufficient to carry BTC toward the psychological $100,000 level. Failure to hold the $82,000–$83,000 support region, meanwhile, could weaken the short-term structure and shift attention toward lower support levels.

Saylor’s four-year bull-market outlook is a longer-term thesis, not a guarantee that Bitcoin will rise continuously. The cryptocurrency could experience sharp corrections even if a broader upward trend develops. Changes in monetary policy, institutional flows, and investor appetite for risk could all influence its path.

For now, the Bitcoin price prediction rests on two distinct considerations: Saylor’s expectation that the next bull market has begun and the market’s ability to confirm that view through sustained price gains. His forecast provides a clear target and timeframe, while technical indicators offer a framework for tracking progress.

Whether BTC reaches $100,000 within 12 months will ultimately depend on market conditions rather than any single executive’s prediction. Investors following the latest Bitcoin price news should distinguish between an optimistic long-term outlook and evidence of a confirmed breakout. Technical indicators and price targets can help frame that assessment, but neither guarantees future performance.

title: President Trump to Highlight Crackdown on Overseas Crypto Scams
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

President Trump to Highlight Crackdown on Overseas Crypto Scams
Trump to tout seizures of fraudulent crypto sites at White House cybercrime event as FBI data shows $11.3 billion in U.S. crypto fraud losses in 2025.
This post President Trump to Highlight Crackdown on Overseas Crypto...
content:
President Donald Trump will use a White House event on Wednesday to spotlight his administration’s push against foreign criminal networks that lure Americans into fake crypto investments, a White House official told Reuters.

The remarks are part of a broader event on cyber crime prevention. Trump and members of his cabinet plan to point to the government’s seizure of fraudulent crypto investment websites and its work to shut down online impersonation scams, the official reportedly said.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, FBI Director Kash Patel, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Attorney General Todd Blanche are expected to attend.

The event follows a March executive order in which Trump directed the Justice Department to prioritize the identification and prosecution of online scammers. He followed that with a memo directing the Department of Homeland Security to work with private companies to surveil foreign criminal hacking groups.

Record losses in internet and crypto scams

The numbers behind the crackdown are grim. Americans filed more than one million complaints with the FBI about internet scams in 2025, a 17% increase from 2024, and reported record losses.

Crypto fraud accounted for more than half of that damage. The FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center logged 181,565 crypto-related complaints and $11.366 billion in losses for 2025, making digital assets the single most loss-heavy category in the report. Crypto investment scams drained $7.2 billion of that total.

The FBI traced much of the activity to organized criminal enterprises in Southeast Asia — in Cambodia, Laos and Burma — that use victims of human trafficking as forced labor inside scam compounds. Criminals make contact through text messages, social media, dating apps and digital ads before steering victims to fake platforms that display fabricated profits. When victims try to withdraw, scammers demand taxes and fees and vanish.

Americans aged 60 and older bore the heaviest burden, with $4.43 billion in crypto-related losses. Crypto ATM scams produced $389 million in losses, a 58% jump from 2024, and recovery scams that target prior victims generated another $1.4 billion.

The global picture is worse. Chainalysis data from January showed illicit crypto addresses received at least $154 billion in 2025, a 162% increase from 2024. North Korea-linked hackers stole $2 billion over the year, including the $1.5 billion Bybit exploit, the largest crypto heist on record.

Enforcement has produced some solid results. The FBI’s Operation Level Up notified 3,780 victims of active crypto investment fraud in 2025 and saved an estimated $225.8 million. A Scam Center Strike Force that combines the DOJ, FBI, Secret Service, State Department and Treasury’s OFAC targets the Southeast Asian compounds.

According to Reuters, Trump and his sons have added at least $2.3 billion to the family fortune from their main crypto ventures, while the investors they courted have absorbed a $2.3 billion hit. 

In October 2025, Trump pardoned Changpeng Zhao, the Binance founder convicted after the exchange pleaded guilty to failing to maintain an effective anti-money laundering program.

Democrats in Congress have accused the Trump family of using the presidency to enrich itself through its crypto ventures, a charge the White House rejects.

White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly said that “all actions by President Trump and his administration are taken in the best interest of the American people.”

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Brex Capital Is Expelled by Financial Commission Two Months After Rebrand
summary:
Brex Capital has lost its Financial Commission membership after repeatedly failing to comply with the organisation’s rules and guidelines. 
According to the Financial Commission’s announcement, the expulsion took effect on 19 October and applies to the broker under both its current name and its form...
content:
2026-10-21T16:02:48.317+02:00

Wednesday, 21/10/2026 | 14:02 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Clients are no longer eligible for the Commission’s Compensation Fund, which can pay up to €20,000 per eligible complaint.
  • QRS Global clients continued using their accounts after the rebrand, but MISA still lists a licence cited by Brex Capital under the QRS Global name.

Brex Capital has lost its Financial Commission membership after repeatedly failing to comply with the organisation’s rules and guidelines.

According to the Financial Commission’s announcement, the expulsion took effect on 19 October and applies to the broker under both its current name and its former name, QRS Global.

Clients Lose Access to the Compensation Fund

The decision ends a membership that began in September 2025, when the broker still operated as QRS Global. The Commission did not specify which rules or guidelines the broker had breached.

Brex Capital continued to promote its Financial Commission membership after the rebrand, telling clients they could seek independent dispute resolution and compensation of up to €20,000 per complaint. The expulsion removes a benefit the broker had continued to advertise under its new name.

Brex Capital’s Links to QRS Global

Brex Capital is an Asia-focused CFD and forex broker. It adopted its current name in August 2026 after what the company described as an acquisition by “an international investment group.”

At the time, new CEO Sophie Squillacioti told Finance Magnates that ownership and the brand had changed, while QRS Global’s trading infrastructure, services and operations continued.

Existing QRS Global clients could continue using their accounts under the Brex Capital brand without registering again, a company representative told Finance Magnates. The QRS website also redirected visitors to the new broker.

Brex Capital’s website says its South African entity is authorised by the Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) and lists a licence from the Mwali International Services Authority (MISA) in Comoros under number T2023349. However, MISA’s register still names QRS GLOBAL LLC as the holder of that licence and marks it active.

The Financial Commission has not linked the expulsion to the change of ownership or the licence listing. Its decision concerns the broker’s access to the Commission’s dispute-resolution and compensation scheme, not the status of its regulatory licences.

title: Strive’s SATS: How 15% Yield Becomes A Bitcoin Accretion Machine
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Strive’s SATS: How 15% Yield Becomes A Bitcoin Accretion Machine
On the accretive potential of the SATS preferred stock. 
This post Strive’s SATS: How 15% Yield Becomes A Bitcoin Accretion Machine first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Allard Peng.
content:
Strive’s newly IPO’d SATS perpetual preferred stock introduces an interesting opportunity: the company could potentially issue preferred equity above its $100 stated amount and grow Net Bitcoin Per Share (Net BPS) in each issuance round, subject to risks and parameters described below. 

This article discusses how and why it works. The key question is whether SATS will trade above $100. Its unusually high 15% fixed dividend makes that outcome, and the subsequent accretion, plausible.

Why SATS could trade above par

SATS carries a fixed annual dividend of $15 per share, based on its $100 stated amount and its 15% number. It ranks junior to Strive’s SATA preferred stock, but its dividend structure offers investors two attractive features. 

First, SATS dividends are cumulative. Strive can defer payments, but any unpaid dividends accumulate as an obligation to preferred shareholders. 

Second, the $15 annual dividend is fixed. This differs from SATA, which currently pays an annualized $13 per share but uses a variable dividend rate. Therefore, SATA shareholders could receive less income in the future if Strive reduces that rate. SATS dividends accrue at a fixed $15 per share per year, but are payable only “when, as and if” declared by Strive’s board, and may be deferred. 

These features could make SATS particularly attractive to investors seeking predictable long-term income.

Consider Strategy’s STRD, the company’s juniormost preferred. STRD currently trades around $71 per share, 29% below its $100 stated amount. Its fixed $10 annual dividend translates into an effective yield of 14%. STRD dividends are also non-cumulative, meaning Strategy can skip payments without creating an obligation to repay those amounts later.

Admittedly, Strategy has significantly stronger Bitcoin asset coverage supporting STRD than Strive has supporting SATS. In fact, STRD’s 4.7x BTC Rating has twice as much asset coverage as SATA, Strives most senior instrument. 

That said, many income investors may place greater weight on dividend reliability than on coverage ratios. SATS offers cumulative dividends and a substantially higher stated yield, creating a reasonable case for the market to price its effective yield below that of STRD.

For example, if investors bid SATS to a 13% effective yield, its market price would reach $115.38.

This leads to an interesting financing opportunity for Strive.

The Net Bitcoin Per Share opportunity

Suppose SATS trades at $115 and Strive issues another 1 million shares through an at-the-market offering.

Strive raises $115 million in gross proceeds and buys Bitcoin.

However, under a Net BPS methodology that deducts preferred stock at its $100 notional amount, those new shares create only $100 million in additional preferred claims.

The remaining $15 million flows directly into the calculation of net Bitcoin attributable to common shareholders.

Under these parameters, Strive effectively raises $115 of capital for every $100 of preferred notional it creates. The annual dividend remains $15, producing an effective financing cost of 13.04% on the capital raised.

Strive can achieve this accretion without issuing additional common shares.

There is one caveat to mention: SATS has a floating liquidation preference that adjusts based on recent market prices. If SATS trades at $115, its liquidation preference can rise toward $115, temporarily increasing the economic claim held by preferred shareholders. However, liquidation preference can also reset downward. The formula references the previous trading day’s closing price during periods surrounding new issuance and the average closing price over the preceding 10 trading days, subject to a $100 floor. If SATS subsequently trades at $100 for 10 trading days, its liquidation preference returns to $100. 

While SATS trades above par, the higher liquidation preference offsets some or all of the apparent economic accretion. Once the preference returns to $100, the company retains the additional capital raised above par while the preferred liquidation claim falls back to its stated amount. 

But here’s the thing. The exact liquidation preference number only becomes relevant if the company is going to liquidate. And this would only happen if the company goes bankrupt. But if the company goes bankrupt, the preferred stock will almost certainly go below $100, which would make the liquidation preference return to $100. In other words, the caveat of the floating liquidation preference actually does not matter when you look at everything in context—it is perfectly valid to use $100 per share as the de facto notional value to compute Net BPS. (Note also that Net BPS is defined by Strategy, and not a metric explicitly reported by Strive. Strive’s prospectus also identifies tax risks that may arise if shares are issued above the liquidation preference, including deemed distributions, disqualified preferred stock treatment, and fast-pay stock treatment.)

The above-par issuance premium can therefore become genuine residual asset value for common shareholders, when we consider the Net BPS metric. 

This could possibly be one of the main reasons Strive decided to go as high as 15%. The high dividend gives it a greater chance of going above par and enabling the aforementioned mathematically guaranteed Net BPS accretion. 

15% Cost of Capital? 

Of course, this strategy relies on the market price of SATS.

At $115, Strive effectively raises capital at a 13% annual dividend cost. At $100, that cost rises to 15%. At $90, the effective cost climbs to 16.67%, while issuance also becomes dilutive under a Net BPS calculation.

Strive should therefore exercise considerable discipline when issuing SATS through an ATM program. Locking mid-to-high-teens costs of capital would only work out well if the return on capital from Bitcoin is massive and if volatility drag does not become a big issue. 

Strive also intends to maintain an 18-month dividend reserve equivalent to $22.50 per SATS share, adding another capital allocation consideration. 

Assuming the company maintains 18 months of dividend coverage, it would need to set aside $22.50 for each share it sells. Assuming it sells at par, that means 22.5% of the money raised must sit in cash equivalents while the remaining 77.5% can be deployed into Bitcoin. Therefore, we can see that the true cost of capital when accounting for the drag of being able to use only 77.5% of your financing is higher than the effective yield at which shares were issued. 

All these considerations need to be managed carefully. 

The key question

SATS may become one of the most expensive digital credit instruments on a stated dividend basis, while simultaneously becoming one of the more attractive financing tools for the Net BPS metric.

If investors consistently value SATS at an effective yield below 15%, then Strive could issue shares above par, purchase additional Bitcoin, and may generate Net BPS accretion under this methodology.

If SATS struggles to maintain a premium, this situation would not apply.

The opportunity lies in the difference between the $100 stated amount and the price income investors are willing to pay for a fixed, cumulative $15 annual dividend.

That spread could become a valuable source of accretion for ASST shareholders.

Strive did not review this article before publication. This article was written by Allard Peng and reflects the author’s own opinion. Scenarios, prices, and yields are hypothetical illustrations, not predictions or guarantees. “Net Bitcoin Per Share” is the author’s methodology, not a Strive-reported metric. Third-party data is as of 21 October 2026 from Strategy.com, Strive.com. 

This article is for informational purposes only. It is not investment, legal, or tax advice, or an offer or solicitation to buy or sell any security. SATS Stock is offered only by Strive’s prospectus supplement and accompanying prospectus; read them, including the risk factors, before investing. Investing in preferred stock and bitcoin-related securities carries substantial risk, including loss of principal and the risk that dividends are not declared or paid.

Allard Peng

Research and Insights Analyst at Bitcoin for Corporations

content:

Wednesday, 21/10/2026 | 12:56 GMT by M4Markets

Disclaimer

  • M4Markets wins Best Trade Execution APAC at iFX EXPO Asia 2026.

M4Markets left iFX EXPO Asia 2026 in Hong Kong with the Best Trade Execution APAC award at the UF AWARDS APAC 2026. During the event, Nastia Kuo also shared her perspective on how AI and human expertise can work together to improve client service.

The recognition follows a recent Best IB Programme award at Forex Expo Dubai, acknowledging another important part of the business: its relationships with introducing brokers.

In Hong Kong, M4Markets speaker, Nastia Kuo, focused on the practical role of AI in everyday client interactions. For Nastia, personalisation should mean understanding what a client needs, what has already happened, and where a process has become difficult.

“AI can help us respond at scale. Trust is built in how we handle the moments that need a human,” Nastia said.

Nastia also highlighted the importance of a smooth transition from automated assistance to personal support. AI can help pass the context of a client’s enquiry to staff, allowing them to focus on clear explanations and thoughtful, individual attention.

These discussions come as M4Markets continues to expand its international partner network, including relationships across Asia, while maintaining a focus on client service and satisfaction. Participation in Hong Kong gave the team an opportunity to meet partners, exchange perspectives, and continue discussions about future cooperation.

M4Markets is proud to receive the “Best Trade Execution APAC” title and thanks its clients, partners and everyone who supported the company through their votes.

About M4Markets

M4Markets is an international online broker offering forex, commodities, indices, shares, and cryptocurrency CFDs through the MetaTrader 4 and MetaTrader 5 platforms. The company provides multilingual client support and works with introducing brokers and partners internationally. Products and services are subject to the relevant legal entity, jurisdiction, and client eligibility.

title: Why centralized exchanges refuse to list legacy crypto tokens without explicit SEC immunity
summary: Vault12 raised $17.45 million selling VGT in 2018 and says it met or dropped every promise, yet the token has never traded on a centralized exchange.
content:
Oct 21, 2026, 8:12 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • Vault12 says exchanges want assurance the SEC won’t later challenge a token’s exit from securities rules before listing it.
  • The firm raised $17.45 million selling VGT in 2018 and says it met or dropped every promise, yet the token has never traded on a centralized exchange.
  • Vault12 wants filings to become conclusive if the SEC doesn’t object within 60 days, a fix it says would give exchanges certainty to list.

The issuer of a cryptocurrency token that has never traded on a major exchange has presented an early test of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission’s (SEC) proposed safe harbor framework.

Crypto wallet backup firm Vault12, backed by Winklevoss Capital and Naval Ravikant, warned that the SEC’s proposed token safe harbor could leave exchanges unwilling to list tokens because of the risk of a later regulatory challenge.

The safe harbor is part of the SEC’s Regulation Crypto Assets proposal, issued in August to establish conditions under which a token would no longer be subject to its original investment contract.

Vault 12 raised $17.45 million from 38 investors through agreements for future tokens in 2018 and detailed how Vault Guardian Token (VGT) has never traded on a centralized exchange, it said in in a comment letter on Tuesday.

The letter presents questions about the SEC’s proposed path for older crypto projects to move their tokens out of securities treatment.

Vault12 says its 2018 token sale fits that path almost exactly: it has fulfilled or formally abandoned every commitment in its white paper, yet its token has never been listed. Its concerns echo a comment letter from industry group The Digital Chamber, which Vault12 says it supports.

Exchanges Vault12 approached about listing VGT wanted assurance that the SEC would not later challenge the token’s status, according to the letter. The company argued that the proposed safe harbor does not provide enough certainty for them to proceed.

The SEC’s proposed Regulation Crypto Assets would create exemptions for token fundraising and a conditional safe harbor for ending an investment contract associated with a token. To use the safe harbor, issuers would have to complete or permanently stop promised essential managerial efforts, make no new such commitments and have no intention of doing so.

They would also file a transition report, known as Form TR, explaining their conclusion, according to the SEC’s proposal.

Vault12 said exchanges considering a VGT listing repeatedly raised the same question: “How do we know the SEC won’t later say VGT is still subject to the old investment contract?”

The SEC’s proposal says the agency could challenge whether an issuer met the safe harbor’s conditions. If a certification was inaccurate, the regulator could conclude that the investment contract had not ended and securities-law requirements continued to apply.

The proposal also says the safe harbor would not prevent other parties from asserting that a token was subject to an investment contract or was otherwise a security.

Vault12 suggested an alternative 60-day window for SEC objections, after which a properly filed certification would become conclusive for the agency, subject to exceptions including fraud or material misstatements.

title: Japanese visitors may be able to pay with yen stablecoins in South Korea under Shinhan-SBI pact
summary: The collaboration will explore card-linked merchant payments for Japanese visitors in South Korea and peer-to-peer wallet transfers among broader cross-border trade remittances.
content:
Summary

  • South Korea’s Shinhan and Japan's SBI are testing yen-backed stablecoin payments for cross-border transactions and trade settlement.
  • The collaboration will explore card-linked merchant payments for Japanese visitors in South Korea and peer-to-peer wallet transfers.
  • While at an early stage without a set commercial timeline, the initiative builds on Shinhan's broader digital asset push with Visa.

Japanese visitors to South Korea might one day be able to transact using yen stablecoins linked to payment cards following experiments conducted by South Korean card issuer Shinhan Card and subsidiaries of the Tokyo-based financial services company SBI Holdings.

Shinhan Card, a unit of Shinhan Financial, is working with cryptocurrency exchange SBI VC Trade and trade finance blockchain company SBI XDC Network APAC to explore yen-backed stablecoin payments between the two countries, SBI Holdings said.

The companies will also study wallet-to-wallet transfers and the use of stablecoins to settle cross-border trade payments. Their work will include systems to detect suspicious transactions and meet anti-money laundering rules.

The process remains at an early stage. The firms have not named the stablecoin they plan to test or set a timeline for trials, let alone a commercial launch.

SBI already distributes JPYSC, a yen-backed stablecoin issued by SBI Shinsei Trust Bank and introduced with Startale Group in June. The token had about 20.1 billion yen ($127 million) in circulation as of Sept. 7, according to SBI VC Trade.

JPYSC is limited to SBI VC Trade accounts and cannot yet be moved to external wallets. Its circulation on public blockchains also depends on legal and tax clarity and regulatory approval. The companies have not said whether JPYSC will form part of the test program.

Shinhan Card, which serves around 20 million cardholders, said it would link the project to Shinhan Financial’s broader digital-asset push, which includes an August agreement with Visa to explore stablecoin issuance, transfers and card settlement.

title: Bitcoin risk management grows more popular as the 'just bet on price' era fades
summary: Your day-ahead look for Oct. 21, 2026
content:
Updated Oct 21, 2026, 7:18 a.m. EDTPublished Oct 21, 2026, 7:15 a.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

This is an excerpt from CoinDesk newsletter 'Daybook.' Sign up here, if you haven't already.

Bitcoin BTC$84,459.46 options are taking a bigger share of the largest cryptocurrency’s derivatives market in a sign that trading is becoming more sophisticated.

According to Volmex, the issuer of the bitcoin volatility index BVIV, options accounted for just under 60% of open interest among all bitcoin derivatives last week. That’s up from around 50% at the start of the year.

Open interest is the total value of contracts that traders have opened and not yet closed. The market encompasses bitcoin futures, perpetual futures and both bitcoin-native and ETF-based options.

Volmex called the growth a structural shift in bitcoin markets, a sign that trading bitcoin is now about managing risk, not just betting on direction.

Options allow investors to hedge their holdings, earn additional income or bet on a big move without borrowing, so positions can last longer than a leveraged perpetual bet. They are also priced on expected volatility, which is what gauges like Vomex’s BVIV track.

Options are derivative contracts with a fixed expiry date that let traders bet on three things at once. They can bet on the direction of the price, on how big the swings will be and on timing, meaning by when a move will or won't happen.

As of Friday, the bitcoin derivatives market looked like this: Options tied to U.S. bitcoin exchange-traded funds had about $36 billion in open interest, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for nearly $35 billion of the total. Add in options on crypto-native platforms, and the figure rises to roughly $76 billion. When bitcoin futures, including perpetual futures and dated contracts, are taken into account, the overall market reaches about $129 billion.

ETF options alone are now about 47% of the bitcoin options market, which is mainly owned by Deribit. IBIT options have tripled since January 2025, when open interest was about $11 billion.

The growth in options is consistent with the pattern seen on U.S. equities, where options tied to the S&P 500 Index accounted for nearly 75% of all derivatives linked to the index and index equivalents as of last year.

The growing use of options is also visible in BlackRock’s expanding lineup of bitcoin-related funds. In June, the world’s largest asset manager introduced the iShares Bitcoin Premium Income ETF (BITA), which seeks monthly income by selling call options on a portion of its IBIT holdings, sacrificing some upside in exchange for option premiums. This week, it filed to offer a bitcoin buffer ETF that uses options to limit losses during a downturn, while also capping potential gains.

All of this suggests bitcoin’s volatility could continue to decline, a trend that has been underway since spot bitcoin ETFs debuted in early 2024. Stay alert!

Read more: For analysis of today's activity in altcoins and derivatives, see Crypto Markets Today . For a comprehensive list of events this week, see CoinDesk's "Crypto Week Ahead."

What’s trending

  • SpaceX and Tesla explore merger that would unite more than 30,000 bitcoin (CoinDesk): Elon Musk said independent committees are assessing a potential merger that would combine the companies’ 30,221 BTC.
  • Solana’s Alpenglow, its biggest network overhaul since 2020, goes live Wednesday (CoinDesk): Solana’s upgrade is scheduled to cut transaction finality from roughly six seconds to about 150 milliseconds by moving validator voting off-chain.
  • Zcash developers confirm November date for upgrade that triples payment speed (CoinDesk): Developers selected an activation point around Nov. 5 for NU7, which would cut block times to 25 seconds from 75 seconds. The change still requires integration into deployment specifications and node software.
  • JPMorgan sees 10% annual bitcoin returns, topping stocks, bonds and gold over next decade (CoinDesk): JPMorgan put a number on bitcoin returns for the first time, forecasting about 10% a year over the next decade. The bank remains cautious about BTC’s role in portfolios.

Today’s signal

The chart shows bitcoin’s daily price swings in candlestick format. Overlaid is the Ichimoku cloud, an indicator used to identify support and resistance and momentum, and the 50-day average price.

Bitcoin looks to have bounced off support at the Ichimoku cloud. For chart analysts, staying above the cloud and the 50-day moving average would signal that the bullish bias is still in place.

The immediate resistance is around $87,500, the recent high, followed by $90,000, a level with large options open interest on Deribit.
