title: Probly Wraps Up TOKEN2049 Singapore and WHALE3RA, Strengthening Its Presence in On-Chain Prediction Markets
summary: The British Virgin Islands, Road Town, October 2026 — Probly, an on-chain prediction market for sports, politics, crypto, finance, and global events, has concluded its participation as a Gold Sponsor of TOKEN2049 Singapore and co-host of the WHALE3RA Afterparty alongside BloFin, TxFlow, and other ec...
content:
The British Virgin Islands, Road Town, October 2026 — Probly, an on-chain prediction market for sports, politics, crypto, finance, and global events, has concluded its participation as a Gold Sponsor of TOKEN2049 Singapore and co-host of the WHALE3RA Afterparty alongside BloFin, TxFlow, and other ecosystem partners.

Across TOKEN2049 week, Probly connected with traders, builders, infrastructure teams, partners, and Web3 communities around the growing role of prediction markets as a way to express views on real-world events.

The week also gave Probly an opportunity to introduce its approach to prediction markets to a broader crypto-native audience: simple access, broad market coverage, self-custody USDC, peer-to-peer trading, and verifiable on-chain settlement.

From Market Opinions to On-Chain Signals

Prediction markets are increasingly becoming an interface for turning expectations about future events into market signals. For Probly, TOKEN2049 provided an opportunity to bring that idea directly to an audience already accustomed to trading changing market conditions, information, and expectations.

The name Probly comes from “probably,” the word people use when the outcome of an event remains uncertain. It is also inspired by P(A), the mathematical notation used to represent the probability of an event.

Probly currently supports 5,100 events and 47,000 markets across Sports, Geopolitics, Crypto, Finance, Economy, and Politics. The platform also offers 172 active live markets for same-day trading, including high-frequency Crypto “Up or Down” rolling markets across BTC, ETH, SOL, and XRP.

Probly is the first prediction market application developed through TxFlow Improvement Protocol 3 (TIP3). Settlement through TxFlow enables on-chain settlement, automatic USDC payouts, and no manual claim step.

Bringing the Prediction Market Conversation to WHALE3RA

Probly also co-hosted WHALE3RA at MARQUEE Singapore during TOKEN2049 week alongside BloFin, TxFlow, and other ecosystem partners.

The event brought together traders, builders, funds, exchanges, infrastructure teams, and Web3 communities, giving Probly an opportunity to engage directly with many of the audiences shaping the next generation of crypto products.

For Probly, these conversations reinforced an important direction for the product: prediction markets should not be limited to occasional major events. They can become a more active interface for following changing information, forming a view, and trading expectations as events develop.

What Comes Next for Probly

Following TOKEN2049 Singapore, Probly will continue developing its prediction market experience around accessibility, broader event coverage, frequent trading opportunities, and transparent on-chain infrastructure.

The company will also continue working with ecosystem and infrastructure partners as it develops new ways for users to express views on future outcomes through on-chain markets.

TOKEN2049 and WHALE3RA marked another step in bringing Probly’s core idea to a wider audience: uncertainty is everywhere, and markets can make collective expectations around what happens next more visible, transparent, and useful.

Before It Happens.

About Probly

Probly is a prediction market built on TxFlow L1 through TxFlow Improvement Protocol 3 (TIP3). It turns views about future events into continuously updated market signals across sports, crypto, economics, news, culture, weather, and other real-world categories.

Probly combines real-time markets, broad event coverage, fully on-chain settlement, and self-custodied USDC infrastructure. Its mission is to make collective expectations more immediate, transparent, and useful by converting uncertainty into a price.

Join over 300 million global users — create your Binance account today and start trading with 0.1% fees.

Binance Global vs Binance US

The main difference between Binance Global and Binance US is that they are actually separate legal entities that follow different sets of rules. 

You can use the global Binance platform version if you live outside the United States, and it has the full list of over 500 coins and high-leverage futures. The US version is built specifically for American residents to meet the strict requirements of US financial regulators. Well, because of these strict laws, the US platform has fewer coins (around 150) and does not offer derivatives like futures or options trading.

Also, on Binance Global, you can easily deposit and withdraw dozens of fiat currencies through bank transfers, credit or debit cards, and third‑party payment services. Binance US currently does not offer cash deposits or withdrawals (limited only). US users rely on ACH transfers and wire transfers for limited fiat support, and these may carry higher fees.

How Does Binance Work?

The Binance platform works by acting as a middleman that connects people who want to buy crypto with people who want to sell it. You can easily create an account, deposit funds, and then you use the exchange’s order book to place your trades. The system then uses its matching engine to pair your buy order with someone else’s sell order at the best possible price. Once the trade is complete, the assets are transferred between internal wallets.

You will notice that your account is divided into several sub-wallets based on what you are doing. You have a Spot Wallet for regular buying and holding, a Futures Wallet for leverage trading, and an Earn Wallet for your savings. You can move your money between these wallets instantly and for free. Basically, this structure helps you keep your different trading strategies organized so you don’t accidentally spend your long-term savings on a risky day trade.

What are the Pros and Cons of Binance Exchanges?

The pros of Binance include support for 500+ cryptocurrencies, competitive fees, advanced trading features, and strong security. While, the cons of the Binance exchange are the Binance US version for Americans with fewer features, overwhelming for beginners, and regulatory issues in the past. 

Advantages of Binance

  • 500+ Listed Cryptocurrencies to Choose From: Binance Exchange offers more than 500 tradable coins for all its customers. This gives crypto traders and investors many options. They can decide to trade or buy popular tokens, meme coins, GameFi, and even AI coins. But if you are in the United States using Binance.US, you have fewer options, around 150 coins to choose from.
  • Multiple Trading Pairs: Binance has over 1,300 trading pairs from which traders can choose. Some of these pairs include BTC/USDT, BTC/FDUSD, XRP/USDT, ETH/USDT,  USDC/USDT, SOL/USDT, and many more.
  • Competitive Fees: Compared to other crypto exchanges like Coinbase or Kraken, Binance offers low trading fees (0.1% maker/taker), so you don’t have to worry about paying a significant portion of your investments and earnings on transaction fees. Additionally, you can get 25% discounts if you use the Binance coin, BNB.
  • Multiple Trading Options and Order Types: Binance Exchange offers various trading options, including peer-to-peer, margin, and spot trading. The platform also has many order types, including limit order, market order, stop-limit order, stop market order, trailing stop order, and post-only order.
  • Robust Security and KYC: Binance enforces various security measures to protect users. For instance, the platform requires a strong password during registration and 2FA for all sensitive operations, such as logging in and transferring funds. They also encrypt data in storage and in transit to ensure that only you can access your personal information. Plus, in addition to these measures, Binance has a strict Know-Your-Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) policy.
  • Supports Fiat-to-crypto: Binance users can easily convert their local currency into digital assets. Some supported fiat on Binance include GBP, AUD, BRL, EUR, USD, ZAR, and RUS. You can make these fiat-to-crypto deposits using bank transfers, online banking, e-wallets, credit/debit cards, and Google/Apple Pay.
  • User-Friendly Mobile app: The Binance app is available for iOS and Android with a simplified Lite mode for beginners and an advanced Pro mode for traders. The app also integrates the Web3 wallet, NFTs, and Earn features.

Want access to 500+ cryptocurrencies and advanced trading tools? Register your Binance account now and start trading in minutes.

Disadvantages of Binance

  • Binance US is Limited: Binance US is a separate exchange operating under different regulations for Binance traders in the United States. Due to these strict regulations, the platform is more limited than the global exchange. It supports about 150 coins and 170+ trading pairs. It was established in 2019, and it is only available in 38 states; traders in Hawaii, Texas, New York, and Vermont cannot use the platform. Also, you cannot trade futures or invest with a margin account on Binance.US.
  • Binance Exchange May be Confusing for New Users: Binance offers advanced trading features, multiple supported cryptocurrencies, and Web3 services. While this may be exciting for experienced traders, it can be confusing for people who are new to the crypto space. In fact, even traders who are familiar with the platform might feel overwhelmed due to all the options available.
  • Lawsuits and Regulatory Trouble in Multiple Countries: Binance has faced many regulatory and legal issues in multiple countries. In November 2023, Binance and its CEO, CZ, pleaded guilty to unlicensed money transmitting and anti-money laundering violations charges. This happened a month after Binance paused all U.S. dollar deposits, withdrawals, and trades in response to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) lawsuit filed against Binance.US on June 5, 2023.
  • Custodial Risk: Although Binance offers self‑custody through its Web3 wallet, most of the users keep their funds on the exchange for trading. In November 2022 and October 2023, there were hacks against the BNB Chain (around $570 million), and earlier in 2019, hackers stole about 7,000 BTC from the exchange. Obviously, Binance covered the losses through the SAFU fund, but these incidents eventually show that even big exchanges are not immune to security breaches.

Who Is Binance Best For?

Binance is best for active day traders, altcoin investors, passive income, high-volume traders, and tech-savvy beginners.

  • Active traders: People who trade often and require deep liquidity, low fees, and sophisticated tools. You see, the large selection of pairs, high leverage, and advanced order types can easily attract day traders and professional investors.
  • Altcoin enthusiasts: Generally, those looking to buy or sell lesser‑known cryptocurrencies or take part in new token launches through the Launchpad will find more options on Binance than on most competitors.
  • Yield seekers: If you want to earn passive income on your crypto, Binance offers numerous staking, lending, and yield farming products with competitive returns.
  • High‑volume traders: VIP tier programs reward high trading volumes with lower fees and better borrowing rates. Plus, corporations or trading firms can also open institutional accounts with dedicated support and portfolio margin programs.
  • Tech‑savvy beginners: It has the Lite interface and educational resources like Binance Academy, so new users can start with simple buys and gradually explore more advanced products.

If Binance fits your trading goals, open your account today and activate your referral bonus before placing your first trade.

What are Binance Fees?

The Binance fees include spot trading charges (0.1% maker/taker), futures trading fees (0.02% maker, 0.05% taker), zero deposit fees, and variable withdrawal fees (depending on the network).

Deposit Fees

The platform generally does not charge you any fees to deposit cryptocurrency into your account. You only have to pay the network fee to the blockchain when you send the coins from your personal wallet.  Unlike crypto deposits, fiat deposits involve third-party payment providers. The table below summarizes the core fees for retail users (both crypto and fiat deposit fees):

Deposit methodBinance Global
Bank transfer (SEPA, FPS, ACH)Free for most currencies. SEPA bank deposit is usually free; Faster Payments Service (FPS) in the UK is free.
Debit/credit cardCard deposits cost around 1.8-2% of the amount. Apple Pay and Google Pay have similar rates
Third‑party payments (Simplex, Banxa, etc.)Fees vary by service, typically around 1-3%
Crypto depositFree; network miners’ fee paid by sender

Withdrawal Fees

Binance crypto withdrawal fees are not fixed, and they change based on which coin you are moving and how busy the network is. You will find that withdrawing Bitcoin usually costs a $5-$10, but withdrawing tokens on the BNB Chain (previously Binance Smart Chain) or Solana can cost less than 50 cents. Actually, the exchange updates these rates regularly to make sure they match the actual blockchain costs.

Withdrawal methodBinance Global
Bank transferSEPA withdrawals cost around €1-€1.50; wire transfers cost $15; some regions are free.
Debit/credit cardNot available for withdrawals.
Crypto withdrawalOnly the network fee is charged

Spot Trading Fees

Binance spot trading charges are based on a tiered system, from regular users to VIP 9. Now, for regular users, a 0.10% maker and taker fee is charged for spot trading. 

Your fees reduce slightly if you are trading USDC. Makers still pay the standard rate, but takers pay 0.095%. If you increase your trading volume over 30 days or hold a significant amount of BNB in your account, your spot trading fees will drop to as low as 0.011% / 0.023% maker-taker. (check screenshot below for exact discount details and VIP tiers)

Futures Trading Fees

Futures trading has a separate fee schedule because the volumes are usually much larger than spot trading. Makers, who provide liquidity to the book, pay as little as 0.02%, while takers pay around 0.05%. You also get a 10% discount on futures fees if you pay using your BNB balance. Right now, these are some of the lowest derivatives fees you can find on any major centralized exchange.

Margin Trading Fees

Binance margin trading has two cost components: trading commission (same as spot rates) and interest on borrowed funds. These rates change every single day based on how many people are borrowing that specific coin. Generally, USDT interest rates might be around 5% to 10% per year, while smaller altcoins might be much more expensive.

Staking and Earn Fees

The Binance platform does not usually charge a direct fee for you to participate in staking or the Earn programs. But instead, the company takes a small percentage of the rewards that the blockchain pays out before they give you your share. So, this means the APY (Annual Percentage Yield) you see in the app is the net amount you will actually receive. Binance.US, however, deducts a 9.95% to 39.95% service fee from staking rewards.

What Are the Best Features of Binance?

The best features of the Binance exchange are advanced trading features, staking services, launchpad, user-friendly mobile app, passive income options, web3 wallet, cloud mining, and an NFT marketplace. 

Binance Trading Features

The top Binance trading features are spot trading, margin trading, futures trading, options trading, copy trading, and automated trading bots.

Binance Margin Trading

Binance margin trading allows you to borrow funds to increase your position size. Binance offers isolated margin (up to 10x leverage), where the collateral is tied to one trading pair, and cross margin (up to 5x). There is also cross margin pro for institutional and high‑volume users that raises leverage to 20x. Higher leverage increases both potential profits and losses.

Here, margin loans generally accrue interest every hour, and rates depend on the coin you borrow (as discussed earlier). Binance also uses a “Smart Liquidation” engine that gradually reduces your positions instead of closing them all at once. There is also Portfolio Margin. It lets you use combined balances across spot, margin, and futures to lower margin requirements and support large leveraged trades.

Binance Spot Trading

Binance spot trading means you can buy and sell crypto directly with market or limit orders. Spot trading pairs include crypto‑crypto pairs (e.g., BTC/ETH), crypto‑fiat pairs (e.g., ETH/EUR), and stablecoin pairs (e.g., BNB/USDT). 

The interface allows you to view order book depth, price charts, and trade history. Generally, spot trades settle immediately, and you own the underlying asset.

Now, if you are a more advanced trader, Binance provides more advanced features for the spot market to support order types and charting features. These features allow you to set limits, market, stop-limit orders, and more. You can read our in-depth Binance spot trading review for more info.

Binance Futures Trading

Binance futures trading lets you bet on whether the price of a coin will go up or down without actually owning the coin itself. It offers USDT‑margined perpetual contracts, coin‑margined perpetual contracts, and delivery futures with expiry dates. 

You can use much higher leverage here, sometimes up to 125x for certain pairs. Binance also provides tools such as isolated and cross margin for futures, take‑profit and stop‑loss orders, bracket orders, and a risk calculator. Check out our Binance futures review article for more details.

Binance Options Trading

Binance options trading gives you the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell a coin at a certain price before a certain date. You can trade European‑style options settled in USDT, and these options have a set strike price and expiry time. The platform has a very simplified options interface that makes it easier to understand than the ones used in traditional stock markets. 

Now, because they are European options, you cannot exercise early, and the platform also offers a simple options widget called “Vanilla Options” for beginner use. 

Binance Copy Trading

Binance copy trading allows you to follow the strategies of other experienced traders. Basically, you can choose a lead trader, allocate funds, and then the system automatically mirrors their trades. 

Here, lead traders earn a 10-30 % share of the profits, and they must maintain consistent performance to remain in the program. You can copy in two ways: fixed amount, where you invest a specific sum, and fixed ratio, where your position sizes follow the same ratio as the lead trader’s positions. 

There is also an “Elite Trader Program” that requires at least 300 copy traders and $750,000 in assets under management. Copy trading supports both spot and futures markets. Also, you can stop copying at any time and withdraw your funds. There are no restrictions.

Binance Trading Bot

Binance offers built-in bots that can trade for you 24/7 based on rules you set. Here are some top Binance trading bots:

  • Spot Grid Bot: This one can place buy and sell orders around a set price range, profiting from sideways markets by buying low and selling high.
  • Futures Grid Bot: Similar to spot grid but for perpetual contracts. So, it will use leverage.
  • Arbitrage Bot: It will exploit price differences between funding rates or futures and spot prices.
  • Rebalancing Bot: This bot generally keeps your portfolio balanced by periodically adjusting allocations to maintain target ratios. You can set the coins and percentage distribution, and the bot rebalances at regular intervals or when price thresholds are met.
  • Auto‑Invest Bot: Implements dollar cost averaging by automatically buying selected coins at fixed intervals. You can choose daily, weekly, or monthly frequency and have the option to earn interest on unspent stablecoins.
  • Spot DCA Bot: This bot buys increments of a coin when the price drops by a set percentage and sells increments when the price rises by a set percentage. It helps manage volatility.
  • Futures TWAP/VP Bots: The bot will execute large orders over time using time‑weighted average price (TWAP) or volume participation (VP) strategies to minimize market impact.

Binance Staking

Binance staking allows you to earn rewards just by holding certain coins in your account. The platform handles all the technical work, and you just click a button to start earning interest. You can choose “Locked Staking” for higher returns if you don’t mind locking your coins there for a set time, or “Flexible Staking” if you want to be able to withdraw them whenever you want.

Binance takes a 10% cut of rewards on popular coins such as Ethereum and Solana. There is also ETH 2.0 liquid staking, which provides a token called WBETH that represents your staked ETH and accrues staking rewards. Explore our Binance staking review article for more info. 

Binance Launchpad

Binance Launchpad is a platform for new cryptocurrency projects to raise capital through token sales. You can participate by holding BNB in your account. The number of tokens you can buy depends on your average BNB holdings over a snapshot period (often 7–30 days) and the project’s allocation rules. 

Binance calculates your ticket based on hourly snapshots of your BNB balance, and at the end of the subscription period, winning tickets are drawn, and BNB is deducted from your wallet to purchase the new tokens. Check out our full Binance launchpad review here.

Binance Mobile App

The Binance mobile app offers two modes: Lite for beginners and Pro for experienced traders. The Lite version displays simple buy/sell options, price charts, and a portfolio overview. The Pro version provides full order books, margin and futures trading, advanced charting, and access to copy trading, bots, and Earn. 

The app also integrates with the Web3 wallet, so you can access DeFi and NFTs within the same interface. It has all the top security features, like biometric login (fingerprint/face), device management, anti‑phishing codes, and the ability to freeze your account from the app.

Binance Earn

Binance Earn is basically a high-yield savings account for your crypto. You can put your coins into various products like “Simple Earn” or “Dual Investment” to get a better return than just letting them HODL in your wallet. Now, within Earn, you will find:

Binance Web3 Wallet

Binance Web3 Wallet is a self‑custodial cryptocurrency wallet built into the Binance mobile app. The wallet uses multi‑party computation (MPC). Here, your private key is split into multiple shares. So, one share stays on your device, one stays on Binance’s servers, and the last one is saved in your personal cloud (such as iCloud or Google Drive). 

Now, you need at least two shares to sign a transaction, so neither you nor Binance can move funds alone. The wallet supports multiple blockchains, including BNB Chain, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, and more. It also has a dApp browser so you can interact with DeFi, yield farms, NFT platforms, and games within the app. Here is the full Binance Web3 wallet review.

Binance cloud mining allows you to earn Bitcoin (BTC) without having to buy expensive mining hardware yourself. Binance has its own marketplace where you can buy, sell, and even create your own Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs). After that, Binance will ask you to complete your verification. Click “Continue” to start the verification process.

Step 5: Finally, once you finish the KYC verification process, it can generally take a few hours to two days to have your account verified and ready for use.

Follow the steps above and register your Binance account now to claim up to $100 in crypto rewards.

How to Deposit to Your Binance Trading Account?

To deposit fiat on Binance, you need to go to the “Deposit” section, choose your local currency, select a payment method, enter the amount, and wait for confirmation.

To deposit crypto on Binance, you need to select the cryptocurrency, copy the deposit address, and send the funds from your external wallet.

Fiat Deposits

  • Choose your currency: Log in, go to Wallet > Fiat and Spot > Deposit, then select your local currency (USD, EUR, GBP, INR, etc.).
  • Select a payment method: You can choose bank transfer (SEPA, SWIFT, ACH, FPS), card deposit, or third‑party services. Now, for example, if you are in India, you might use IMPS or a UPI transfer; in Europe, you would use SEPA; in the US, you can use ACH or a debit card (available only on Binance US).
  • Enter the amount: Now, you need to type how much you want to deposit and follow the instructions to complete the transfer. Here, for card deposits, you will be redirected to the payment processor, and bank transfers require you to send money to a Binance bank account with your reference code.
  • Wait for confirmation: Generally, bank transfers may take hours or days; card deposits are instant. Once funds arrive, you will see them in your Fiat and Spot wallet.

  • Choose the crypto: Go to Wallet > Fiat and Spot > Deposit, then select your desired coin (e.g., BTC, ETH, USDT).
  • Select network: Binance generally supports multiple networks for many coins, so for instance, USDT can be deposited via Ethereum (ERC‑20), BNB Chain (BEP‑20), Tron (TRC‑20), or Arbitrum. 
  • Copy the deposit address: Binance generates an address, so you need to copy it and paste it into the sending wallet. Also, some coins require a memo or tag (e.g., for XRP, XLM), and if you forget the memo, your deposit may be delayed. So, check that too.
  • Send the funds: Now, you can initiate the transfer from your external wallet, and after network confirmations, the deposit will appear in your Binance wallet. Well, deposits are usually credited after one or two confirmations for major coins; smaller networks may take longer.

  • DeFi and AI Coins: The exchange lists hundreds of project tokens for Artificial Intelligence and decentralized finance.

Binance Security Review: Is It a Safe and Legit Crypto Exchange to Trade?

Yes, Binance is a legit and safe crypto exchange. It uses industry‑standard security measures and has a large insurance fund. Here are its most advanced security systems:

  • Proof of Reserves (PoR): Binance publishes Merkle tree proofs showing that the exchange holds reserves equal to users’ balances. So, you can verify your own balances on the PoR page by generating a leaf of the Merkle tree, and the audit covers major assets like BTC, ETH, USDT, and BNB.
  • Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU): Binance created the SAFU in 2018. It is an insurance fund seeded with trading fees and acts as a backstop in case of hacks or extreme events. Currently, at the time of writing, Binance converted SAFU holdings to BTC, worth about $1 billion. The company pledged to top up the fund if its value falls below $800 million.
  • Cold storage: The majority of user funds on Binance are kept in cold wallets not connected to the internet, and only a small portion remains in hot wallets for daily withdrawals.
  • Risk engine: Binance uses an automated risk engine to monitor accounts and block suspicious activity. Basically, it includes real‑time transaction monitoring, geofencing, and anti‑money laundering (AML) procedures.
  • Withdrawal whitelisting: Binance also has an address whitelisting feature that restricts withdrawals to only pre-approved addresses. When you enable this feature, your account can only send funds to these whitelisted addresses. This will prevent unauthorized access and losses in a phishing attack or hack.

Trade with confidence on a platform backed by Proof of Reserves and a $1B SAFU fund — create your Binance account today.

But yes, Binance has also faced many regulatory issues in various countries. But besides regulatory issues, it has also been involved in scandals and significant lawsuits, like the one filed against Binance.US by the SEC in June 2023. 

Also, Binance and its CEO, Changpeng Zhao, pleaded guilty to anti-money laundering violations and other charges on November 21, 2023. Binance agreed to pay $4.3 billion to settle charges, while Changpeng Zhao stepped down as CEO and agreed to pay $50 million toward the settlement.

Can Binance be Trusted?

Yes, the Binance exchange can be trusted because it has a long history of protecting users and following international financial standards. You might hear about legal battles in the news, but the company has always worked with governments to resolve these issues and improve its systems. 

There are over 300 million registered users globally without any problems, which is obviously a very strong sign of reliability. Actually, the company has survived many “crypto winters” and market crashes while remaining the number one exchange in the world. But still, it’s a custodial platform. title: Gold Price Recovers Intraday Losses, but Technical Charts Keep Bearish Trend in Focus
summary: On Oct. 20, gold prices continued to be pressured as three charts indicated prices were around $4,120 to $4,133.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XAU

On Oct. 20, gold prices continued to be pressured as three charts indicated prices were around $4,120 to $4,133.

Market data showed a daily loss, but with some gains in intraday trading. TradingView’s daily chart was bearish, and the money-flow indicator was bearish. The latest readings focused on local levels of support and their level of strength, as well as how strong the recovery would be.

Gold remains below earlier trading levels

Gold was trading at $4,133.00, up $7.52, or 0.18%, as of the last bell on Investing.com. The prices were lower than $4,180 before reaching the latest reading. The graph also contains a few short-lived rebounds in the decline. But those recoveries have not been enough to bring the trading range back to its previous levels.

The intraday chart shows that the lower prices of the session were close to $4,110. Source: Investing.com

Gold touched back this price zone after a short testing move, but the trend continued. The new increase pushed prices back up to $4,133. The movement was an upswing from the lowest point in the session, but did not form a lasting upward movement.

The technical chart shows a broader downward trend

Gold price had risen from $16.40 to $4,124.52 at the time of the chart on the TradingView Daily chart. It had a price drop in its history, dropping from prices above $ 5,200 in March. It then proceeded through a number of lower trading ranges before coming back to levels around $4,100 in October.

Gold also saw a resurgence in August as prices rose toward $4,600. But the progress was reversed during September when sales resumed. Source: TradingView

Prices then trended toward $4,200 and remained within a fairly tight range in October. The latest daily candle showed a high of $4,147.10 and a low of $4,111.60.

Chaikin Money Flow – Traders saw the same chart on TradingView with a reading of -0.06 for the Chaikin Money Flow. Under this indicator calculation, selling pressure in the market did not exceed buying. The temperature was still below freezing at the latest measurement. However, the direction of the indicator cannot be used to determine prices in the future.

TradingEconomics records further intraday volatility

Gold’s price in the TradingEconomics chart was $4,122.20, a $18.70, or 0.45% decrease on the daily chart. The five-minute chart showed the price of the stock bouncing back and forth between $4,110 and $4,150. The movements demonstrated that gold was making rapid movements within the session.

The price dropped from about $4,148 and then rallied back up to $4,145 in the early part of the period shown. Source: TradingEconomics

Gold later drifted down to $4,120 as a further plunge was experienced. The market then bounced around that level again, followed by short rebounds. Prices pushed higher towards $4,130 near the right side of the chart and pulled back.

The prices and percentage changes shown were different on the three platforms due to the difference in snapshots and the chart settings. They should thus be considered as independent readings, and not market prices. However, the three charts all positioned gold in their immediate vicinity at the $4,100 to $4,150 level.

Nearby support and resistance remain in focus

The charts were hovering at the lower end of the trading range in recent times and placed a 4,110-4,120 range there. This could be a focus point should prices drop further. Any break below the range may lead to more selling of gold. The provided charts, however, do not validate a breakdown below the support level.

The positive side is that $4,140 to $4,150 is a close range where traders can keep an eye on. Gold will have to break up above this range and continue to hold that level to show a better short-term rally. The daily chart also revealed that trading was around the $4,200 level earlier this week, which offers another reference level.

The charts currently available do not show or define how much or what causes the market to move into negative territory or what direction to go next. Traders can keep an eye on price action, trading volume, and money flow readings for extra signals. Other factors that can affect the price of gold include economic releases, interest-rate anticipation and the movement of the US dollar.

The decline needs to be confirmed separately before it is possible to explain it with the above-mentioned factors. As of press time, gold was trading around $4,120 to $4,133 on the chart snapshots provided. Daily price action was stuck in a downward trend, and intraday rebounds continued to demonstrate price volatility.

title: Switzerland Clears First Retail Bitcoin ETF, Unlocking Direct BTC Access Nationwide
summary:
Key Takeaways: FINMA issued its first retail ETF based on Switzerland’s first direct investment into Bitcoin. The regulator allowed the exemption from the diversification guidelines due to Bitcoin’s long trading
The post Switzerland Clears First Retail Bitcoin ETF, Unlocking Direct BTC Access Nation...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • FINMA issued its first retail ETF based on Switzerland’s first direct investment into Bitcoin.
  • The regulator allowed the exemption from the diversification guidelines due to Bitcoin’s long trading history and liquidity.
  • Despite Bitcoin’s volatility, it needs to be accompanied by high risk disclosures, custody protection, and suitability checks, warns FINMA.

The Swiss decision introduces another major step towards regulated crypto investing. Switzerland’s Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) has licensed the nation’s first Bitcoin (BTC) exchange-traded fund (ETF) that can invest directly in BTC and be made available to retail investors.

  • FINMA Opens Direct Bitcoin ETF Access to Retail Investors
  • Bitcoin Wins an Exemption From Diversification Rules
    • Custody and Crypto Risk Controls Take Center Stage
    • Swiss Rules Demand Clear Bitcoin Risk Warnings

FINMA Opens Direct Bitcoin ETF Access to Retail Investors

FINMA said growing demand for cryptocurrency investments, particularly Bitcoin, contributed to its decision.

The approved product is designated as an “other fund for alternative investments” in Swiss law with specific risks. The new structure is a regulated retail fund, which invests directly in Bitcoin, and it is one of the structures not already available in Switzerland which have been approved.

No information regarding the fund manager was provided by FINMA, nor was a launch date. But other issuers are also currently applying or announcing Bitcoin ETFs, the regulator noted.

The move broadens the base of investors by allowing individuals other than a professional investor to buy and sell index funds. The crypto fund, which was mainly targeted at qualified investors, received authorization from FINMA in 2021, a precursor to more regulated digital asset exposure.

Read More: Bitwise Launches First U.S. Spot NEAR ETF With 5% Staking Rewards and $32B Intents

Bitcoin Wins an Exemption From Diversification Rules

A particular aspect of the approval is FINMA’s ruling that exempts the approval-holder from the standard risk-diversification requirements.

It’s typical to expect traditional investment vehicles to be diversified. But a Bitcoin ETF focuses investment solely on one cryptocurrency.

In the reason provided for its exception, FINMA cited Bitcoin’s relatively long trading history as well as its high volume of trading when compared to other digital assets. That enables the fund to still be directly exposed to Bitcoin, but within the regulated frame of Swiss funds.

Custody and Crypto Risk Controls Take Center Stage

The approval has a number of restrictions on investors’ protection. Bitcoin custody risks, operational risks and other risks are things that financial institutions that handle the ETF must deal with. In the past FINMA has provided guidance on how supervised firms should improve safeguards for crypto assets, including measures for the prevention of asset loss.

Fund documents should also explicitly disclose the risks involved in the security, in addition to delving into the ways in which it differs from a traditional diversified fund.

Bitcoin’s own market risk remains if it is approved, emphasized FINMA. The btc exchange is highly volatile and investors may lose a big fraction of their capital, said the regulator.

Read More: Tokenized iShares MSCI South Korea ETF Arrives on StonkFun for Solana Coin Launches

Swiss Rules Demand Clear Bitcoin Risk Warnings

The distribution of the ETF will be governed by Switzerland’s Financial Services Act, better known as FinSA. This involves providing explicit warnings for the volatility and losses of Bitcoin and a suitability assessment where appropriate.

The design serves both goals – regulated access of retail investors to direct exposure to Bitcoin and the introduction of regulation for fund managers and distributors.

There are now already more Bitcoin ETF applications on the waiting list, and FINMA’s decision could pave the way for others to come on top of the Swiss regulatory framework for these new direct crypto investments.

title: Circle CPN Wins Money20/20 Bronze With 175+ Financial Institutions Driving Network
summary:
Key Takeaways: Circle Payments Network (CPN) has been named Bronze for Payments in the Money20/20 awards. Circle stated over 175 financial institutions assist to scale up CPN into a global
The post Circle CPN Wins Money20/20 Bronze With 175+ Financial Institutions Driving Network appeared first on C...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Circle Payments Network (CPN) has been named Bronze for Payments in the Money20/20 awards.
  • Circle stated over 175 financial institutions assist to scale up CPN into a global payments network.
  • CPN revealed in previous reports that it would have $14.7B in annualized transaction volume at the end of Q2 2026.

Circle has attained new clarity and endorsement for its stablecoin payment initiative, with Circle Payments Network (CPN) earning Bronze at the Money20/20 awards. The company emphasized that it has an expanding institutional base, as it has over 175 financial institutions behind the network.

  • Circle Highlights 175+ Institutions Behind CPN
  • CPN Reached $14.7 Billion in Annualized Payment Volume
    • Circle Pushes Stablecoins Deeper Into Financial Infrastructure

Circle Highlights 175+ Institutions Behind CPN

Circle announced the award on X, thanking both its payments team and the financial institutions helping build CPN.

Circle Payments Network (CPN) just won BRONZE in Payments at the @money2020 Money Awards.

Thank you to the 175+ financial institutions helping make CPN a global payments network, and to the Circle payments team for building it. https://t.co/C2GoBARFVl

— Circle (@circle) October 19, 2026

The 175-plus number is similar to that of Circle, which reported 175 financial institutions at the end of June 2026. This was up from a 24% rise in the previous one.

Note that not all schools will necessarily be running active payment processing, although if they have enrolled this should mean they are. The firms are assisting in globalizing CPN, but Circle’s award announcement didn’t give a new breakdown of active transaction participants.

CPN aims to link financial institutions, payment providers and fintech firms via stablecoins-based settlement systems, with USDC being the key point of value transport across borders.

Read More: Circle Brings USDC and EURC Into SAP Workflows Powering 84% of Global Commerce

CPN Reached $14.7 Billion in Annualized Payment Volume

Based on transactions completed over the last 30 days of the quarter, CPN now reports the number of annualized transactions at $14.7 billion, according to circle. The figure was up 76% quarter over quarter.

This shouldn’t be interpreted as the annual volume of settlement, but as the annualized number. It is also called the sales velocity of the transactions and is the rate of transactions in the reference period forecasted for 12 months.

Separately, Circle also reported that an additional $14.8 trillion worth of USDC was transacted onchain in Q2, and that by the end of Q2, there were $73.3 billion worth of USDC in circulation, indicating much deeper USDC activity outside of CPN as a whole.

Circle Pushes Stablecoins Deeper Into Financial Infrastructure

Circle is testing out CPN expansion to make it easier for traditional finance institutions to settle with stablecoins.

Its Managed Payments service enables banks and payment companies and fintech platforms to connect with one another in their existing fiat value chain, and Circle to handle the underlying asset minting, burning, blockchain infrastructure and compliance.

All that structure has been created to lighten the burden on institutions which would like to settle with stablecoins but do not wish to maintain crypto assets.

Circle has also been increasing by way of partnership with Games across large markets when it comes to providing payout connectivity. The firm has stated that Nium settled USDC with more than 190 countries’ payout infrastructure before.

The other corridor partner firms include those that are building payouts in the United States, European Union, India, Philippines, Singapore & the United Arab Emirates.

Now that stablecoins are starting to challenge traditional banking methods, particularly with bank settlement, payments for merchants, payroll systems, and global payout systems, Money20/20 is another feather in the cap for Circle.

title: Metaplanet Wins Approval for 2,100 BTC Deal to Build Nasdaq Bitcoin Treasury Giant
summary:
Key Takeaways: All of the proposals related to Metaplanet’s 2,100 BTC investment were approved by Super League shareholders. Following the cierre, about 93.7% of the renamed Superplanet is expected to
The post Metaplanet Wins Approval for 2,100 BTC Deal to Build Nasdaq Bitcoin Treasury Giant appeare...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • All of the proposals related to Metaplanet’s 2,100 BTC investment were approved by Super League shareholders.
  • Following the cierre, about 93.7% of the renamed Superplanet is expected to be held by Metaplanet.
  • The partnership adds approximately N70m in Bitcoins to the new trading platform for treasury assets listed on the Nasdaq.

Super League shareholders have paved the way for Metaplanet’s largest Bitcoin expansion. The approved transaction will add 2,100 BTC to the company and $2.5 million in cash, which the company expects to rebrand as Superplanet in the future.

  • Metaplanet’s 2,100 BTC Deal Clears Shareholder Vote
  • Five-Year Lock-Up Signals a Long-Term Bitcoin Strategy
    • Super League Will Become Superplanet With Nasdaq Ticker SUPA
    • Warrants Could Unlock Billions in Additional Capital

Metaplanet’s 2,100 BTC Deal Clears Shareholder Vote

Super League announced that shareholders approved every proposal presented at its October 16 annual meeting, including the strategic investment from Metaplanet.

At the closing of the deal, Metaplanet will donate $2,5 million in cash and 2,100 Bitcoins from its U.S. subsidiary to Sapperstone. Comparing the value of the Bitcoin was calculated at approximately $132.1 million at the August 14 price, but by the time of writing, it was about $170 million.

Metaplanet, in return, will acquire 44.86 million common shares valued at $3 per share, 100 shares of convertible perpetual preferred shares and long-dated warrants.

Following the transaction, Metaplanet will hold positions representing approximately 93.7% of the Company’s common shares based on Super League’s total shares outstanding as of September 29.

Read More: Coinbase and Marqeta Bring 24/7 Stablecoin Card Spending to Millions of Merchants

Five-Year Lock-Up Signals a Long-Term Bitcoin Strategy

Metaplanet is required to hold a five-year lock-up period with respect to common shares for sale at closing and common shares that may be issued upon the exercise of warrants and preferred stock.

In addition, Metaplanet holds a governance right with their strategic preferred shares. Large issues, such as some changes to its charter, mergers and transaction of control, would require its consent.

The transaction is likely to close during the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to usual conditions and necessary upcoming filings with the Nasdaq.

Super League Will Become Superplanet With Nasdaq Ticker SUPA

Immediately after the closing, Super League will become Superplanet, Inc., and will trade on the Nasdaq under the symbol SUPA.

It still has its advert and media business which will remain as it is, and it is developing a Bitcoin treasury strategy around the 2,100 BTC donation.

With the addition of the structure, Metaplanet also has a fully listed platform on the U.S. exchanges as well as the Tokyo Stock Exchange, providing access to both dollar and yen-based capital markets.

Read More: Arc Mainnet Goes Live With 190+ Partners, BlackRock and Visa Back New Network

Warrants Could Unlock Billions in Additional Capital

In addition to this, Metaplanet will also be granted warrants for 10 years with maximum 381 million common share warrants that will have an exercise price of $3 to $33.50.

Dylan LeClair, director of Bitcoin strategy at Metaplanet, told CFM Media that the warrants can be valued at a potential $3.4 billion in equity capital. Metaplanet also will withhold 100 percent of its funds for 24 months in the form of junior preferred stock.

Super League stockholders have approved every proposal at last week’s annual meeting, including:

✅ Issuance of common stock and warrants to Metaplanet
✅ Name change to Superplanet, Inc. ($SLE -> $SUPA)
✅ Increase in authorized preferred shares from 10m to 100m

At closing, Metaplanet will contribute 2,100 BTC + $2.5m USD in exchange for 44.86m common shares, 100 shares of Strategic Alliance Preferred Stock, and common stock warrants representing up to ~$3.4b of potential equity capital.

Based on the ~3.0m Super League shares outstanding as of September 29, Metaplanet would own ~93.7% of Superplanet’s common stock at closing. All shares to be held by Metaplanet are subject to a five-year lock-up.

The Strategic Alliance Preferred carries no preferred dividend or liquidation preference; its purpose is governance. While Metaplanet holds it, Metaplanet’s consent is required for charter amendments, mergers or changes of control, and designation of a board majority.

As outlined in the proxy, Superplanet intends to grow BTC per share primarily by issuing senior, non-convertible perpetual preferred stock rather than debt.

Metaplanet will also hold a 24-month right to subscribe for up to $210m of unlisted Junior Liquidity Support Preferred Stock. If issued, it would pay SOFR + 4.00% and rank junior to any senior preferred Superplanet may issue, allowing Metaplanet to provide subordinated capital in support of the balance sheet.

A new chapter begins soon. 🇺🇸🪐

— Dylan LeClair (@DylanLeClair) October 19, 2026

Ramping up Bitcoin per share will be the main method for Superplanet to do so, rather than pushing traditional debt usage heavily, providing Metaplanet with a second lever to assess Bitcoin’s U.S. corporate strategy.

content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Strive successfully closed an IPO of an upsized $630 million, in its perpetual preferred stock.
  • SATS pays 1.5% compounded on a $100 stated value, payable on each business day.
  • Strive received new funds from the offering which could go towards future Bitcoin investments; the specific amount of Bitcoin was not specified.

Strive has gone one step further in the public markets with its Nasdaq listing of SATS, a new perpetual preferred security on the basis of fixed income and corporate stakes in Bitcoin. The company sold a total of 7 million shares of SATS at $90 a share, grossing $630 million.

  • Strive’s SATS IPO Brings in $630 Million
  • Daily Dividends Add a Different Structure to Bitcoin Exposure
    • Bitcoin Purchases Remain a Major Possibility
    • SATS Expands Strive’s Bitcoin-Focused Capital Stack

Strive’s SATS IPO Brings in $630 Million

Strive announced the closing of the upsized offering on October 20, with SATS expected to trade on the Nasdaq Global Market under the ticker SATS.

SATS is now listed on Nasdaq.

15.00% fixed annualized dividend rate based on $100 stated amount. Paid every business day.

First dividend: November 9, 2026, inclusive of dividends accrued since the October 20 closing.

$SATS $ASST $SATA https://t.co/uHFnzEW9LN

— Strive (@Strive) October 20, 2026

The preferred shares have a sum of $100 and carry a cumulative dividend at 15% per annum. This annual amount is $15 per share when dividends are declared and fully paid. This is the nominal annual dividend, which corresponds to about 16.7% of the price of the Offering.

Dividend payments will happen every day a business is in operation from November 9, 2026. If the payment is declared in full, it will cover dividends from October 20 when declared.

Read More: Bitwise Launches First U.S. Spot NEAR ETF With 5% Staking Rewards and $32B Intents

Daily Dividends Add a Different Structure to Bitcoin Exposure

SATS is a perpetual product: that is, there is no traditional date of maturity. Strive is pitching the security as a cash flow tool in addition to another favored choice in the capital structure, SATA. For the company, SATS is an additional measure to boost its “Amplification Ratio”, which the firm believes is at the heart of its ability to benchmark better than Bitcoin over time, CEO Matt Cole said.

In addition, Chief Risk Officer Jeff Walton highlighted that Strive has no debt or impending debt due and has no other fixed financial obligations apart from dividends at this time.

Bitcoin Purchases Remain a Major Possibility

Strive has not locked up all of the offering into Bitcoin. The funds received can be applied to general corporate uses, such as Bitcoin purchases, cash flow of working capital, income-producing assets, expenditures on capital, acquisitions, repurchasing shares as disclosed in company notes to regulatory submissions.

With that being said, unknowns remain about who the last Bitcoinmaker will be. The offering, according to outside estimates, is expected to net around $608 million, excluding underwriting expenses and other costs. If all that was invested in Bitcoin, it represents the purchase of more than 7,300 BTC at a representative price of close to $82,500.

Strive has also stated it currently holds 36,818 BTC, which would result in its capital above 44,000 BTC if it fully allocated every BTC stored.

SATS Expands Strive’s Bitcoin-Focused Capital Stack

Since the listing, Strive has obtained a further capital raising mechanism, apart from by way of traditional debt. While Strive continues to go the Bitcoin route on its balance sheet, the main thrust of focus of SATS is predictable income.

The company described the preferred stock as part of a broader family of liquid financial securities aimed at investors seeking different combinations of income, price stability and Bitcoin-linked corporate exposure.

title: The Trades Your Algorithm Rejects May Be the Most  Important Data You Never Measure
summary:
Most trading systems are very good at remembering what they bought.
They record entry prices, exits, profits, losses, holding periods and dozens of other variables.
When a trade succeeds, analysts can study why. When it fails, they can study that too.
But there is another group of decisions that ...
content:
Skip to content

Most trading systems are very good at remembering what they bought. They record entry prices, exits, profits, losses, holding periods and dozens of other variables. When a trade succeeds, analysts can study why. When it fails, they can study that too. But there is another group of decisions that often disappears almost completely: the trades the system rejected.

That creates an important blind spot.

Imagine an automated crypto trading system evaluates 1,000 possible opportunities and rejects 950 of them. It executes only 50 trades.

The developer can carefully analyse the performance of those 50 trades. But that still does not answer a basic question:

Were the other 950 rejections good decisions?

A filter may appear to protect a trading system because the trades it accepts perform reasonably well. But without observing what happened after rejection, nobody can know how many losses the filter successfully avoided or how many potentially profitable opportunities it discarded.

This problem became increasingly important to me while studying algorithmic decision-making on decentralised exchanges.

Rejection is also a decision

A trading system does not make decisions only when it buys or sells.

Choosing not to trade is also a decision.

Suppose a token is rejected because its liquidity is too low. Another is rejected because of wallet concentration. A third fails a momentum threshold.

Twenty-four hours later, the first token collapses, the second becomes inactive and the third rises sharply.

Those outcomes contain information about the filters that made the original decisions.

But if the system stopped observing each token at the moment it rejected it, that information has been lost.

This creates an asymmetry in the data.

Accepted decisions naturally generate histories because capital is attached to them. Rejected decisions can disappear from the record even though they may greatly outnumber accepted ones.

I wanted to measure that missing side of the decision process.

Following what the algorithm rejected

I developed Post-Rejection Follow-up Sampling, or PRFS, as a framework for doing this systematically.

The basic idea is simple.

When an algorithm rejects a candidate, do not throw the candidate away.

Record the decision and continue observing the asset.

The process can preserve the time of rejection, the reason for rejection, the market conditions visible at that moment and subsequent observations at predefined intervals.

The order matters.

The decision comes first. The subsequent market path is observed afterward.

In my PRFS audit, the dataset contained approximately 67,000 forward observations associated with 2,997 rejection events involving 457 unique token mints.

The audit also exposed another important lesson.

Collecting more data does not automatically solve a measurement problem.

The identity of the decision being followed, the timing of observations and the way those observations are connected back to the original rejection all matter.

A large dataset can still answer the wrong question if those relationships are incorrectly recorded.

Making rejected decisions measurable

I also developed RED-2400, a public benchmark designed around algorithmically rejected trading events.

The objective was not to produce another trading strategy or claim that one filter could predict token prices.

It was to make the rejected side of the decision process observable.

Once that information exists, researchers can ask much better questions.

Did a particular filter mostly reject assets that subsequently deteriorated?

Did it repeatedly discard assets that later appreciated?

Did its effectiveness change under different market conditions?

Are several filters rejecting essentially the same population for different reasons?

And perhaps most importantly:

Is a trading system being improved based only on the small fraction of opportunities that the system itself made observable?

Independent developers are beginning to test the idea

One of the most encouraging developments has occurred outside my own research.

Independent developers have since built rejection follow-up ledgers and related post-rejection tracking into their own systems.

Some have created persistent ledgers for rejected signals rather than allowing those decisions to disappear from process memory. Others have implemented post-rejection trackers that continue observing rejected candidates at predefined intervals so that screening rules can later be evaluated against what actually happened.

Other independent researchers have used public data from my work to investigate selection and survivorship bias in their own trading datasets and strategy experiments.

This matters to me because research becomes much more informative when someone other than its author tries to use it.

An external implementation can expose limitations, reveal new applications and sometimes show that an apparently promising strategy should not be deployed at all.

That last outcome deserves more attention.

Sometimes the valuable result is deciding not to trade

Financial research is often presented as valuable when it discovers something profitable.

But identifying something that should not be deployed can also have economic value.

Suppose a strategy looks profitable in historical data.

A broader dataset then reveals that successful assets were disproportionately represented in the original sample. Or a more realistic replay shows that the apparent advantage disappears after transaction costs.

The useful result is no longer a profitable backtest.

The useful result is avoiding a potentially bad decision.

This is especially important in fast-moving crypto markets, where small samples, changing liquidity and selection effects can produce attractive historical results that may not survive real-world conditions.

A system capable of discovering evidence against its own decisions may ultimately be more useful than one designed only to find apparent winners.

This problem extends beyond crypto

Reject-side measurement is not only a cryptocurrency problem.

Consider credit underwriting.

A lender naturally observes repayment performance for approved borrowers. The outcomes of rejected applicants are much harder to observe under the same lending decision.

Consider fraud detection.

Cases that pass through later stages of investigation may generate rich labels, while cases removed earlier in the pipeline can receive much less follow-up.

Similar problems can appear in insurance, risk screening, recommendation systems and other machine-learning applications.

The details differ, but the underlying problem is related.

Automated systems increasingly filter large populations before taking action on a much smaller subset.

If researchers evaluate only the population that survives those filters, they may end up evaluating a population partly created by the system itself.

Build systems that remember their “no”

As financial systems become more automated, I believe their audit trails should preserve more than executed actions.

Rejected decisions should become first-class data.

What did the system see?

Why did it say no?

What happened afterward?

Was the rejection ultimately consistent with the system’s objective?

And does the same rule continue to behave similarly when market conditions change?

These questions become even more important as financial decision-making moves toward machine-learning models and increasingly autonomous agents.

A trading algorithm that records only its trades remembers what it did.

A system that also follows its rejections can begin to measure whether its decisions were actually useful.

The data currently discarded may contain some of the most important information about whether automated financial systems deserve confidence.

This article is for information only and is not investment advice.

Research links

Post-Rejection Follow-up Sampling (PRFS): arXiv:2606.08228

RED-2400: arXiv:2605.12151

About the author

Arati Uday Kamat is an independent researcher working on algorithmic decentralised-exchange trading, reject-side outcome measurement and financial-system evaluation. Her research includes Post-Rejection Follow-up Sampling (PRFS), arXiv:2606.08228, and RED-2400, arXiv:2605.12151, a public benchmark for studying rejected trading decisions.

title: Casper – Why AI Agents Need Their Own Payment Rails
summary: Michael Steuer is President and CTO of the Casper Association, the Swiss non-profit behind Casper Network, a proof-of-stake Layer 1 built for regulated real-world assets and payments between AI agents. Born in Amsterdam and based in Los Angeles for more than two decades, Michael has spent around 30 ...
content:
Skip to content

Michael Steuer is President and CTO of the Casper Association, the Swiss non-profit behind Casper Network, a proof-of-stake Layer 1 built for regulated real-world assets and payments between AI agents. Born in Amsterdam and based in Los Angeles for more than two decades, Michael has spent around 30 years in technology. That includes a stint as CTO for mobile at THQ, where his team shipped some of the first downloadable mobile games. He then co-founded Casper in 2018, built much of its ecosystem tooling through his company MAKE, and returned to lead the project in 2024.

The link will open a new window. Click the menu and down arrow to download the file.

Why you should listen

Casper’s origin story starts inside Ethereum’s own research group, where its proof-of-stake design was first developed. Michael and his co-founders wagered that enterprises would need something Ethereum wasn’t going to deliver quickly: a chain that companies with thousands of existing engineers could build on using the languages, testing and deployment processes they already have. Just as important was certainty. Michael explains why the probabilistic finality retail users tolerate, waiting through confirmations before an exchange releases funds, is unacceptable for an institution moving billions. During that window nobody can say who is legally responsible for the money, so Casper was designed so that a transaction belongs to the recipient from the very next block. He applies the same realism to tokenization. Minting a token that claims to represent an asset takes a minute, he says, but making that token confer enforceable rights is the hard part. Through the ERC-3643 standard and the T-REX Network, Casper is working to make compliance data, such as investor eligibility, jurisdictional limits and holding periods, travel with an asset as it moves between chains.

The second half of the conversation turns to what Michael sees as the larger opportunity. Cloudflare now reports that bots generate more web traffic than humans, yet almost no website can sell anything to them. Sign-ups, logins, card forms and terms-and-conditions boxes were all built for people. His answer is x402, a dormant payment code from the early HTTP specification that Coinbase and Circle revived as a standard for agents to pay per request. Casper is a founding member of the x402 Foundation, which now sits under the Linux Foundation, and settles those payments in its own dollar stablecoin, csprUSD. Payouts.com recently adopted Casper as the settlement rail for its AI agent products. Michael argues that companies blocking agents are turning away most of their visitors. He also expects stablecoin tribalism to disappear, because an agent shouldn’t care which dollar it spends.

That emphasis on ease of use is the thread through the final stretch. Michael says crypto’s usage remains in the single-digit percentages of the global population after 16 years largely because the industry made it so hard to use, from seed phrases to incompatible wallets, and warns against repeating that mistake with agents and tokenized assets. He makes the case for the CSPR token as a utility asset whose value tracks network usage, citing a staking yield he puts at around 10 to 11 percent alongside native liquid staking, and the recent Kraken listing for US access. In the hot take round he calls himself a multi-chain opportunist and argues that blockchain should never try to be the answer to everything. He predicts a decade defined by the convergence of TradFi and DeFi and by agentic traffic approaching totality. He also notes that most people don’t realize they can hold tokenized stock exposure in a wallet and borrow against it, and names Foundation as his sci-fi pick.

Prediction markets reflect market sentiment, whereas futures empower traders to capitalize on price action. Most platforms restrict users to one mechanism — prediction venues rarely feature leveraged instruments, while derivatives platforms lack event contracts. Outpoll bridges this divide, delivering both asset classes through a single account, shared balance, and unified application.

TL;DR: The Hyperliquid Policy Center supports the SEC’s proposed crypto framework but says five changes are needed to make the rules workable for token developers and markets.

The Hyperliquid Policy Center has welcomed the US Securities and Exchange Commission‘s attempt to clarify how securities law applies to crypto assets, while warning that details around distributions and trading could still create unnecessary barriers.

In a comment published October 19, the group urged the regulator to revise its proposed Regulation Crypto Assets framework in five areas. Its concerns include how administrative steps in token airdrops are treated, how tokens can trade after an exempt distribution, and whether a safe harbour offers clear enough protection once a project has matured.

The centre also wants clearer rules for token buybacks and a consistent approach to the interaction between federal exemptions and state securities requirements.

The proposals reflect a long-running problem for cryptocurrency developers. A network token may begin life inside a fundraising arrangement, yet eventually circulate in a system where thousands of participants trade and use it without dealing directly with its original issuer.

Drawing a line between those stages has been difficult under decades-old securities tests. The SEC’s proposal is intended to offer more predictable treatment, but the consultation process shows that industry participants still disagree about where the boundaries should fall.

The advocacy group’s submission is not a regulatory decision. It is one contribution to a rulemaking process whose final outcome will depend on the commission’s response to the evidence and objections it receives.

title: Bitcoin (BTC) Price Prediction: BlackRock’s $663M ETF Inflow Reverses October Outflows—Can BTC Break the $90K Barrier?
summary: Bitcoin (BTC) attracted renewed institutional interest on October 19 as BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded a substantial inflow, helping lift total net flows into US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) into positive territory for the session.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin (BTC) attracted renewed institutional interest on October 19 as BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded a substantial inflow, helping lift total net flows into US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) into positive territory for the session.

The development offered a fresh bullish signal as Bitcoin traded within $81.185–$82,954, although questions remain about whether demand can sustain a move toward $90,000.

Glassnode’s ETF flow data highlighted the surge, while market analysts pointed to Bitcoin’s daily Relative Strength Index (RSI), liquidation levels, and on-chain demand metrics to assess the recovery. Together, these indicators present a mixed picture: institutional buying has strengthened, but broader spot demand remains a key factor in determining whether the latest rebound can develop into a sustained advance.

BlackRock Bitcoin ETF Inflows Lift Market Sentiment

BlackRock’s IBIT attracted approximately $665.2 million on October 19, according to ETF flow data compiled by TFTC. However, outflows from Fidelity’s FBTC and Grayscale’s GBTC reduced the combined net inflow across US spot Bitcoin ETFs to approximately $526.6 million. This distinction matters because IBIT’s individual inflow was larger than the amount ultimately entering the entire ETF group.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs reported $663 million in inflows on October 19, led by BlackRock’s IBIT, though adjusted net inflows were closer to $527 million. Source: Glassnode via X

The daily inflow was the strongest since September, according to the supplied Glassnode analysis, and represented a significant change from the selling pressure seen earlier in October. However, the latest available figures showed that US spot Bitcoin ETFs remained down approximately $90.6 million for the month through October 19. The single-day inflow therefore narrowed October’s cumulative outflows but did not fully erase them.

The figures suggest that institutional demand may be returning, particularly through BlackRock’s fund. Yet one strong session does not establish a durable trend. Continued positive flows across multiple trading days would provide stronger evidence that investors are increasing their exposure to Bitcoin rather than making a short-term allocation.

Bitcoin Price Prediction: RSI Signals a Potential Recovery

Technical analysis shared by market commentator @Wealthmanager showed Bitcoin holding above a key daily support zone, with the 14-period RSI near 46. The indicator measures the strength of recent price movements and can help traders identify changes in momentum.

Bitcoin is holding above key daily support, while the 14-period RSI approaches levels that previously attracted buyers. Source: @Wealthmanager via X

The accompanying chart compares recent price action with earlier RSI divergences, highlighting periods when weakening downside momentum preceded price recoveries. If Bitcoin maintains support and the RSI begins moving higher, the setup could strengthen the case for a recovery. However, an RSI reading near 46 is not, by itself, a bullish confirmation. A sustained momentum shift and a break above nearby resistance would provide clearer evidence.

For the BTC price prediction, the immediate focus remains on whether buyers can defend the current support area and push the price above the recent trading range. Failure to hold support would weaken the recovery setup and could expose Bitcoin to another decline.

Bitcoin Price Faces a Key Test Above $84K

A CoinGlass liquidation heatmap showed Bitcoin advancing from around $81,000 to above $84,000, crossing a price area containing concentrated leveraged positions. Such heatmaps estimate where liquidation orders may cluster, helping traders identify levels where rapid price movements could trigger forced position closures.

Bitcoin’s liquidation heatmap shows a sharp rally from around $81,000 to above $84,000, breaking through a key liquidity level. Source: CoinGlass via X

A move above a heavily populated short-liquidation zone can accelerate gains if bearish traders are forced to close their positions by buying back Bitcoin. However, liquidation clusters do not guarantee a breakout, and the resulting momentum may fade once forced buying subsides.

The $84,000 area therefore represents an important near-term reference point in the supplied chart analysis. A sustained move above this zone could improve the technical outlook, while a rejection may leave BTC vulnerable to renewed consolidation. Reaching $90,000 would require Bitcoin to clear intervening resistance and attract sufficient follow-through buying.

Bitcoin May Be Entering an Accumulation Phase

Crypto analyst @misterrcrypto argued that Bitcoin’s current consolidation resembles the 2022–2023 accumulation period, when the market traded within a broad range before beginning a stronger recovery. The analyst’s chart identified a potential bottoming phase around $81,000 and suggested that prolonged sideways trading could precede another advance.

The attached chart overlays a “bottoming phase” box on 2026-2027 price action around $81,000, mirroring the 2022-2023 consolidation that preceded strong gains. Source: @misterrcrypto via X

Historical comparisons can help frame market scenarios, but they cannot establish that the same sequence will repeat. The duration of consolidation, investor demand, macroeconomic conditions, and the amount of available liquidity can all influence the next major move.

If Bitcoin continues to hold its recent support while buying pressure gradually improves, the accumulation thesis could gain credibility. Conversely, a breakdown below support would challenge the idea that the current range represents a durable market bottom.

Weak Spot Demand Remains a Risk for BTC

CryptoQuant’s apparent demand growth indicator continued to show negative readings in recent months, according to its latest analysis. The metric compares changes in Bitcoin supply with estimated demand to assess whether the market is absorbing available coins. Negative readings suggest that demand has not consistently kept pace with the supply entering circulation.

Bitcoin’s apparent demand growth has turned negative in recent months, indicating weak spot buying as prices consolidate near $80,000 in October 2026. Source: @cryptoquant_com via X

CryptoQuant contributor Rei Researcher noted that Bitcoin had recovered toward $82,000 even as apparent demand remained negative. The analysis indicated that demand had weakened since May 2026 and that short-term improvements had not yet produced a sustained reversal.

This creates an important distinction between a price rebound and a broader recovery. ETF inflows and short liquidations can support upward moves, but stronger spot buying would help demonstrate that investors are accumulating Bitcoin at current prices. Without that confirmation, rallies could remain vulnerable to profit-taking and renewed selling pressure.

Can Bitcoin Break the $90K Barrier?

Bitcoin’s near-term outlook depends on whether institutional inflows continue, technical support holds, and spot demand improves. BlackRock’s latest ETF inflow provides a constructive signal, while the move above $84,000 highlights the potential for derivatives positioning to amplify price changes.

Bitcoin (BTC) was trading at around $82,453 at press time. Source: Brave New Coin

However, the negative apparent-demand readings and October’s still-negative cumulative ETF flows show that the recovery remains unconfirmed. Traders will be watching for sustained ETF inflows, a stronger RSI, and a decisive break above nearby resistance before treating $90,000 as a more immediate target.

For now, $90,000 remains a potential upside objective for BTC price rather than a confirmed destination. A sustained move toward that level would require broader participation from spot buyers alongside continued institutional demand.

TL;DR: Super League shareholders have approved proposals connected to Metaplanet’s plan to contribute 2,100 BTC and cash to a new US-listed Bitcoin treasury platform.

Metaplanet’s proposed American Bitcoin treasury vehicle has moved a step closer to reality, but the transaction has not yet closed. Super League Enterprise said shareholders approved the relevant proposals at their annual meeting on October 16, clearing an important hurdle in the arrangement announced earlier this year.

Under the deal, Metaplanet’s US subsidiary would contribute 2,100 Bitcoin and $2.5 million in cash to Super League. After closing, the Nasdaq-listed company is expected to change its name to Superplanet and trade under the ticker SUPA.

The arrangement gives the Japanese Bitcoin treasury specialist a potential US capital-markets platform, while Super League would retain its existing advertising and media business as an operating segment.

Importantly, the shareholder vote is not the same as completion. Regulatory filings, Nasdaq requirements and other customary closing conditions remain outstanding, with the companies currently targeting the fourth quarter.

The proposed structure also raises questions that extend beyond the Bitcoin price. Investors will need to watch how ownership is allocated, how additional capital could be raised and whether the operating business changes the risk profile of a Bitcoin-heavy public company.

For now, the news is a procedural milestone in an unusual cross-border deal — not evidence that 2,100 BTC has already arrived on the balance sheet.

TL;DR: Bitmine says its Ethereum holdings reached approximately 6.04 million ETH after it added 12,535 tokens over the past week.

Bitmine Immersion Technologies has pushed its Ethereum treasury past the six-million-token mark, reporting holdings of 6,041,481 ETH as of October 18. The company said it acquired another 12,535 ETH during the preceding week.

The size is striking even by corporate crypto-treasury standards. Bitmine describes its position as roughly 4.9% of Ethereum’s circulating supply and says more than five million of its ETH are staked.

That staking component matters. Unlike a Bitcoin treasury that generally depends on price movements, a large Ethereum holding can also earn network rewards by participating in validation. Rewards are not risk-free, however, and the economics depend on staking performance, technical operations and protocol conditions.

Bitmine valued its wider portfolio of crypto assets, cash, marketable securities and other investments at about $15.1 billion. Its holdings therefore represent a substantial bet on Ethereum as both a long-term asset and a productive network.

The company’s disclosure offers investors a clearer look at the scale of that wager, though headline token counts are not the same as shareholder returns. Equity valuation, financing arrangements and the market price of ETH all affect what ownership in the company is ultimately worth.

As more listed firms build dedicated crypto treasuries, those distinctions are likely to become increasingly important.
